characters.description: A Chicago-based criminal-defense lawyer who is quirky and razor-sharp in equal measure. In this series, she moves to New York to oversee a consent decree against the NYPD and ensure that the cops operate within the scope of the law and don't lock up innocent people in the name of case closure. Or so most are led to believe. In reality, the consent decree is cover for her to investigate the precinct's captain, C.W. Wagner, for corruption. For tropes related to her onThe Good Wife, clickhere. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: Elsbeth absolutelydotes onTeddy, but she's also very protective of him, and goes through a very long conversation with Roy, Teddy's boyfriend, for almost 90 minutes. Amoral Attorney: Some of her less-than-honorable actions from her days as a lawyer come back to haunt her in season 2.

characters.name: Elsbeth
characters.description: A Chicago-based criminal-defense lawyer who is quirky and razor-sharp in equal measure. In this series, she moves to New York to oversee a consent decree against the NYPD and ensure that the cops operate within the scope of the law and don't lock up innocent people in the name of case closure. Or so most are led to believe. In reality, the consent decree is cover for her to investigate the precinct's captain, C.W. Wagner, for corruption. For tropes related to her onThe Good Wife, clickhere. Age-Inappropriate Dress: More than one person has called Elsbeth's taste in bright clothing and polka dots more suitable for someone much younger. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: Elsbeth absolutelydotes onTeddy, but she's also very protective of him, and goes through a very long conversation with Roy, Teddy's boyfriend, for almost 90 minutes.

characters.name: Officer (later Det.) Blanke
characters.description: A beat cop in the precinct who quickly takes a shine to Elsbeth. Conflicting Loyalty: In the first season, Kaya is caught in the middle when she finds out Elsbeth is investigating Wagner for potential corruption. Kaya has worked for Wagner for years, respects him greatly, and swears she's never seen him behave in anything except an honorable manner, but she also trusts Elsbeth and knows she wouldn't be poking into this for no reason. To make it more complicated, Wagner is aware Elsbeth is looking into him and has asked Kaya to keep tabs on her for him, while Elsbeth admits she isn't sure Wagner is guilty or not. Curly Hair Is Ugly: Played with. Kaya has long, curly hair, and goes through anExpository Hairstyle Changewhen she gets promoted to detective, having her hair straightened. The implication is that she straightened it to look more "professional." "Friends" Rent Control: While Elsbeth is established as having made a lot of money in Chicago, Kaya is a cop. She's shown to live in a decently-sized house in Queens by herself after she stops rooming with Elsbeth. Put on a Bus:By the end of Season 2, she has taken position in a task force in Washington D.C.

characters.name: Captain Wagner
characters.description: The captain of the precinct, whom Elsbeth is investigating for corruption. Actor Allusion: Season 3 has him playing a trombone, like his character inSeries/Treme. Black and Nerdy: Season 2 reveals that he's a huge space geek. Dirty Cop: Elsbeth is placed within the precinct to see if he is taking bribes from the sweatshop making his wife's clothing and putting a kibosh into any investigation of it. It turns out he is innocent, and Lt. Noonan has been framing him. Do Not Call Me "Paul": Wagner doesn't like being called by his given name, "Charles Wallace", and gets rankled when Celetano dares to say it aloud even if it's in the privacy of Wagner's office. He's also not happy when Elsbeth blurts it out in the bullpen.

characters.name: Lt. Noonan
characters.description: Angry White Man: Noonan believes thatPolitical Correctness Is Eviland that Wagner was promoted above him because of it rather than because ofmerit. Big Bad Friend: Noonan is a close friend to Captain Wagner, who he was also throwing under the bus for his own crimes. Bigot with a Badge: Noonan is aDirty Copwho believes Wagner (apparently a close friend of his) was promoted due to political correctness. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He is a close friend to Captain Wagner, and yet is throwing Wagner under the bus for his own crimes. Broken Pedestal: Wagner considered Noonan to be family, even making Noonan godfather to his children. He's devastated to find out that Noonan was deeply corrupt and setting him up to take the fall.

characters.name: Lt. Connor
characters.description: A lieutenant brought in to replace Dave Noonan and help improve the department's efficiency. Affirmative-Action Legacy: Ironically, given that Noonan's issue is thatPolitical Correctness Is Evil, his replacement is of Asian descent. Asian and Nerdy: He introduces himself as a numbers guy who considersMoneyballhis favorite movie. He also dresses up asWinston Churchillfor Halloween. The Bore: Connor isThe Stoic, inexpressive, and fond of numbers. However, he does eventually warm up to Elsbeth. Everyone Has Standards: Connor may be an introvert who loves technology, but in "Bunker Down" he gives a"The Reason You Suck" Speechto introverted tech guru Craig Harris when he realizes the man is a violent, paranoid misanthrope.

characters.name: Det. Smullen
characters.description: An old-school detective in the department who tends to butt heads with Elsbeth. Inspector Lestrade: He's a competent detective trusted by Captain Wagner. However, he's used to solving straightforward cases and is slow to pick up the plot when confronted with murderers who use elaborate ruses to try and get the police off their scents.

characters.name: Det. Browner
characters.description: A rather aggressive detective who's focused on closing his cases quickly using the most-obvious solutions he sees. Inspector Lestrade: Once he has his sights on a suspect, he's quite dogged in taking that person down. Whenever Elsbeth starts picking his cases apart, he digs his heels and tries harder to reinforce his position. Put on a Bus: As part of Judge Crawford's attempts to get Elsbeth to back off, he gets reassigned to another precinct as part of the layoffs Crawford arranges. Sequel Non-Entity: Each of the detectives Elsbeth works with appears multiple times except Browner, who only appears in "A Classic New York Character" and then isn't seen again. It would beChuck Cunningham Syndromeexcept that his absence isHand Wavedlate in Season 2 (a whole season and a half since his one and only appearance) by saying he got reassigned as part of Crawford's layoffs.

characters.name: Det. Donnelly
characters.description: A detective in the NYPD that often butts heads with Elsbeth. Inspector Lestrade: She thinks she's going after run-of-the-mill murders and not carefully premeditated schemes so she isn't as quick as Elsbeth in spotting the loose threads murderers leave dangling. Not So Above It All: She’s giddy with glee at the mere opportunity to bust a jewelry heist. Pet the Dog:While she had no reason to, she comes to Elsbeth’s fashion show debut to support her in“A Fitting Finale”.In“Elsbeth Flips the Bird”, she (alongs with Buzz and Edwards) happily play poker with Elsbeth despite them usually finding her annoying, showing that off the clock, they can all be friends.In"Ick, A Bod", she encourages Elsbeth to be optimistic that even though she doesn't know her neighbors, they are still looking out for her. While she had no reason to, she comes to Elsbeth’s fashion show debut to support her in“A Fitting Finale”.

characters.name: Det. Edwards
characters.description: An NYPD detective who likes to use the latest technologies in pursuing her cases. Broken Pedestal: She finds herself disappointed to learn that Quinn Powers is a fraud and Cerberus is a scam. Hidden Depths:"Hot Tub Crime Machine"reveals that she is in a polyamorous relationship. Ludd Was Right: Edwards thinks that technology is the way forward in policing and criminal investigations. However, Elsbeth always ends up figuring out the truth using old-fashioned legwork and insightful questioning. Polyamory: As stated above, she is in one such relationship, though she doesn't elaborate much further on it.

characters.name: Det. Fleming
characters.description: An older detective who takes Kaya under his wing as she works towards the detective department. A Day in the Limelight: While he appears a lot,"Scenes from an Italian Restaurant"focuses onThat One Casefor him and gives him significantly more character focus. I Coulda Been a Contender!: Fleming says that his life was completely changed and "the wind was taken out of his sails" by the corruption in the Moresco case. Reluctant Retiree:Almost became this in "Murder from Scratch", to the surprise of everyone including himself. After years of saying all he wanted was to get his pension and retire, the moment it arrives, he doesn't want to leave, in part because of Elsbeth. Wagner advocates for him and gets him job security for a few more years. That One Case: For him, it's his very first case as a homicide detective, the murder of Goldie Moresco. He always figured there was more to it than the Eddie Nova angle, but the department was happy to brush the whole thing off as gang violence.

characters.name: Det. Rivers
characters.description: One of the detectives who handled the investigation into Andy Mertens' murder. As an exchange of favors for the captain of his precinct reopening the investigation, Elsbeth and her precinct have to take him on, which proves to be quite the struggle for them all. Character Development: While he was introduced as aHate Sink, by "I Know What You Did Thirty-Three Summers Ago" he's showing more of an interest in justice and willingness to learn from his colleagues. Clueless Detective: Rivers is screamingly bad as an investigator, always jumping to flimsy conclusions to arrest suspects and working off of shaky evidence on a good day. Even the Loving Hero Has Hated Ones: Due to how much of an unprofessional, rude, and sexist man Detective Rivers is, he is one of the few people that Elsbeth genuinely dislikes, which surprises even herself when she realizes it. She even recommends to Captain Wagner that Rivers get a reprimand and that it go in his permanent file. Freudian Excuse: "Otherwise Enraged" reveals that he wanted to become a cop after his aunt was killed in a hit-and-run when he was twelve.

characters.name: Officer Reese Chandler
characters.description: A beat cop assigned to help Elsbeth Tascioni with her work after Kaya becomes detective. Motor Mouth: He's very chatty at first even for the chatty Elsbeth mentioning among others that he doesCross Fitand that his nana had a glass eye which used to freak him out. The Watson: In his debut episode he shadows Elsbeth and asks questions that help the audience better understand Elsbeth's thought processes.

characters.name: Officer Hackett
characters.description: Cope by Creating: She works through her ideas by crafting, and uses stand-up comedy as her outlet away from being a cop. Insult Comic: Has some traces of this in her act, making some light jokes at the expense of Wagner and Fleming when they show up to her show. Married to the Job: While she likes doing stand up as a release, she is dedicated to her career as a cop.

characters.name: Det. Taylor
characters.description: Ascended Fangirl: Her first case in "Basket Case" investigates the St. Ivan's basketball team and their legendary coach, Coach Willoughby, both of whom she is a fan of. However, she keeps it professional. Played Ball in College: Taylor herself played women's basketball in college, so she knows the ins and outs of the sport when assigned to the St. Ivan's case. Tomboy and Girly Girl: When paired with Elsbeth, especially since their first case involved college basketball (which Nina is well-versed in and Elsbeth is less familiar with) and their second involved a debutante ball (which Elsbeth gets into while Nina criticizes).

characters.name: Teddy
characters.description: Elsbeth's adult son who has decided to move closer to his mom in New York. Alliterative Name:TeddyTascioni. Fatal Attractor: Elsbeth mentions in"Something Blue"that, based on his last few boyfriends, Teddy doesn't really seem to fall for kind or honest people. His new boyfriend Roy in Season 2 is a break from this trend. Following in Relative's Footsteps:Zig-Zagged. Teddy starts out wanting nothing to do with the law since both his parents were lawyers, were rarely around, and, in his view, were supporting a corrupt system. He starts to soften on this stance seeing his mother use her law background to really help people, taking the LSAT and looking into law schools.Judge Crawford's manipulation of the legal system and death as a martyr turns Teddy against it again, but using the same attention to detail as his mother to find evidence against Judge Dousant in the Season 2 finale implied he would play it straight in Season 3. Downplayed in Season 3, as Teddy settles on becoming a journalist, exposing truth by holding those in power accountable, not unlike what his mother does. Unseen No More: ThroughoutThe Good Wifeand Season 1, Teddy was only ever mentioned by Elsbeth in conversation asThe Ghost, but finally appears in person in Season 2's "Gold, Frankincense, and Murder".

characters.name: Claudia
characters.description: Captain Wagner's wife. Nobody Suspects the Woman: Invoked in"I Know What You Did Thirty-Three Summers Ago"when Claudia steals a glass from Milton Crawford, saying he wouldn't know what she was coming.

characters.name: Julia
characters.description: Captain Wagner's eldest daughter. Dating What Daddy Hates: While her first date pick was only objectionable because the man in question was in a relationship, her second choice isDetective Rivers, aHe-Man Woman Haterwidely disliked by Wagner and his entire precinct. She later dumps Rivers because of his constant need for Wagner's approval. Gadgeteer Genius: She comes in to help the precinct (and her father) with tech stuff. Jerkass Ball: In "Otherwise Enraged", Julia gives her father an ultimatum to uninvite her ex, Det. Rivers, from their anniversary party or she won't come, because she was angry her father never ran the idea by her before inviting him. She comes around by the end and realizes she should have talked to Rivers directly and not let her discomfort potentially ruin her parents' celebration or hurt Rivers for no good reason. Infantilization Retaliation: Julia is frustrated that her father still sees her as a little girl when she's 27 years old, and feels like he babies her more than his other children.

characters.name: Agent Celetano
characters.description: A federal agent who is investigating Captain Wagner for corruption. Inspector Javert: He is determined to root out any potential corruption involving Wagner and is unmoved by Elsbeth's pleas to ease up based on her gut instincts.

characters.name: Judge Crawford
characters.description: Arc Villain: In the second season, with him initially getting away with his murder of Andy and causing problems for Elsbeth when she keeps digging into him. Asshole Victim: The man murdered a girl for not wanting to be with him, murdered Andy when having him alive proved too risky for his career, used his connections to sabotage Elsbeth and the people she cared about, and effectively ruined Delia Kirby's life, what with trying to frame her and even destroying her reputation even when she got acquitted. Being locked up for his crimes would have been best, but he certainly worked to earn that bullet. Big Bad: From his appearance in "One Angry Woman", Crawford becomes a villain that looms large over Season 2. Even when he isn't shown onscreen, he's disrupting theNYPDrunning andafter his death, his ally sends Elsbeth to prison. Blue Blood: Crawford is extremely proud of his blue-blooded lineage and is fond of aClass-Based Insultto anyone he views as impeding him. Casting Gag:Michael Emerson(alongside beingCarrie Preston's husband) previously played Leland Townsend, a soft-spoken and evilPsycho Psychologistknown for going up against the main character in the Kings' previous TV series,Evil (2019). Here, he plays an evil judge who once again uses the law to spread misery and get away with his own crimes.

characters.name: Angus
characters.description: A Scottish musician/fireman who witnesses a New York murder from his small village via The Iris interactive installation in "Tiny Town". Accent Interest: According toWord of God, part of Elsbeth's attraction to Angus is his accent isn't one she hears all the time. Firemen Are Hot: Played with. The end of "Tiny Town" reveals that his day job is firefighting, and he is Elsbeth's to-date onlyLove Interest. However, it bothers her as much as she's attracted to him, because Elsbeth knows that firemen are always attracted to her becauseof her red hair. Girls Like Musicians: Elsbeth is charmed by Angus's music. Long-Distance Relationship: Elsbeth and Angus meet via virtual portal, falling in love an ocean apart. They continue to see each other in spite of staying in their respective countries.

characters.name: Alec Bloom
characters.description: Broken Pedestal:When Elsbeth is told there is no evidence Alec was ever homeless as a child, as he states in his campaign platform, her growing admiration of him is dampened. Doppelgänger Replacement Love Interest: Soon after breaking up with Angus, Elsbeth meets Alec at a benefit and they hit it off. Both love interests' names start with an A, they are bothTall, Dark, and Handsome, and they were both firemen at one time. Firemen Are Hot: Downplayed, as Alec is a former firefighter, but he isTall, Dark, and Handsome. No Celebrities Were Harmed: His political platform at least is inspired by that of NYC mayoral elect Zohran Mondani (though he wasn't yet an elect when the episodes were written). Photo Op with the Dog: They seem to be manufactured by Melissa more than by Alec himself, but she certainly takes every opportunity to photograph him doing good deeds, from charity fundraisers to convent food drives.

characters.name: Winnie Crawford
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She seems to want to be friendly with Elsbeth in their first couple of meetings, but the audience sees she is using Elsbeth to get something she wants. Crusading Widow: Winnie is introduced using her husband's good name to support her fundraising efforts. Destroy the Evidence:When Elsbeth tips her off about a piece of evidence that went missing, Winnie goes home, looks through her husband's things, and burns the evidence. Fiery Cover-Up:Winnie burns the final piece of evidence of her husband's linking him to Sherry's murder.

characters.name: Cpt. Tully
characters.description: Fixing the Game:Attempted by Tully in "Murder from Scratch" in order to force Wagner to retire Fleming, but Elsbeth catches on. Villain Has a Point: Tully's reasoning for pressuring Wagner to retire Fleming was based on Fleming's age, since he is close to the NYPD's mandatory retirement age. While Wagner was doing it more as a show of power than anything else, it would not have been a totally unfair way to balance the budget, had Tully not had an ulterior motive.

characters.name: Officer Reynolds
characters.description: Ambiguous Gender: Uses they/them pronouns, but has a feminine name. Commonality Connection: In their debut episode "I See...Murder", Elsbeth initially doesn't gel with Officer Reynolds during the investigation, as Reynolds mostly keeps to themself. Thankfully, the two get a bond over their love of dogs. Contrasting Replacement Character: While Elsbeth and Kaya were friendly and casual when they worked together, Officer Reynolds likes to keep things close to the chest, which Elsbeth struggles with. Eventually Reynolds loosens up enough to get along with her.

characters.name: Officer Chandler
characters.description: A beat cop assigned to help Elsbeth Tascioni with her work after Kaya becomes detective. Motor Mouth: He's very chatty at first even for the chatty Elsbeth mentioning among others that he doesCrossFitand that his nana had a glass eye which used to freak him out. The Watson: In his debut episode he shadows Elsbeth and asks questions that help the audience better understand Elsbeth's thought processes.

characters.name: Dr. Cameron Clayden
characters.description: I Will Wait for You:Zig-Zagged. When Kaya decides to go undercover at the end of Season 2 into Season 3, Cameron agrees to wait for her. When she returns months later and is struggling to get close to him again, he admits that he's not sure he can wait like that again.

characters.name: Prof. Modarian
characters.description: A drama teacher at a college, Alex Modarian, finds himself in deep water when his lead actress plans to go public with their affair, which will particularly hurt him as she is one of his students. Alex is the antagonist of the pilot episode. Bookends:Is the antagonist of the pilot episode and the murder victim in the Season 2 finale. Casting Couch: While his students are usually talented performers, the ones he beds tend to get the better parts and are often demoted once their relationship ends. As one student puts it:"The wider you spread your legs, the bigger your part." Evil Brit: He is the first antagonist inElsbeth, andStephen Moyeruses his natural English accent.

characters.name: Joann Lenox
characters.description: One of New York's top real estate brokers, Joann has her sights set on a building owned by Ms. Gloria Blecher. Unfortunately for her, Gloria refuses to sell, leading her to take more drastic action. Joann is the antagonist of the episode "A Classic New York Character". Extremely Protective Child: She is motivated to kill Gloria because of Gloria's throwing out of her mother and destroying both of their lives over her mother's affair with Gloria's husband. Frame-Up: Part of her and the rest of the board's plan is to set Gloria's son Lewis Jr. to take the fall for the murdernoteNo pun intendedfor the murder, by tricking him into getting his fingerprints on the wrench used to loosen the bolts on the railing. Manipulative Bitch: Joann got the board members on her side by lying that Oprah was interested in the building. When they turn on her when Elsbeth proves their guilt, she calls them out, saying they all hated Gloria, and Oprah's "sale" was just the excuse they needed.

characters.name: The Co-op Board
characters.description: The tenants of Gloria Blecher's building, who have long suffered under the woman's tyrannical rule. When Joann Lenox informed them that acertain celebrityhad her eye on buying the building, they leapt at the chance to sell. However, since Gloria refused to let go of her building for any price, the four banded together with the broker to... remove a certain Gloria-shaped obstacle in their way. The four are the secondary antagonists of the episode "A Classic New York Character". Everybody Did It: A big twist of the episode is that Joann wasn't in on the murder alone, but was working with the four, who each had a part to play:Annie tricked Lewis Jr. into putting his fingerprints on the wrench used to loosen the bolts on Gloria's railing, then stashed said wrench in the dumbwaiter for Joann.Daniel distracted the doorman, Fiznik, long enough for Joann to sneak by him into the building.Leonard arranged for the sidewalk nearby to be repaired, which gave him a reason to put up barriers that would prevent innocent bystanders to be crushed by either Gloria or the railing (and incidentally took out a streetlight with the repairs and made Lewis look guiltier), and allowed Joann into his apartment that was right under Gloria's giving her a way to the railing.Dorothy unmuzzled her dog and allowed him to bark, which drove Gloria to the railing long enough for it to give way. Annie tricked Lewis Jr. into putting his fingerprints on the wrench used to loosen the bolts on Gloria's railing, then stashed said wrench in the dumbwaiter for Joann. Daniel distracted the doorman, Fiznik, long enough for Joann to sneak by him into the building.

characters.name: Skip Mason
characters.description: As the producer of the hit reality showLavish Ladies, Skip Mason soon found himself in a tough spot with one of his stars, Wendy Wexler. She had threatened to reveal that he had driven one of her co-stars into a breakdown that ruined her career and life... unless he gave her creative control of the show. What followed was an impulsive murder and a more impulsive cover-up. Skip is the antagonist of the episode "Reality Shock". Bad "Bad Acting": Skip isridiculouslybad at not seeming super guilty, which is why Elsbeth clocks him for the murderer immediately. It's just a matter of proving it. Bad Boss: Skip generally treats the crew ofLavish Ladieslike dog shit on his shoe, which is why they are so willing to work with Elsbeth to prove his guilt. Bad Liar: Skip repeatedlysays too muchand gets angry during his interviews with Elsbeth.

characters.name: Margo Clarke
characters.description: A matchmaker to the rich and famous, the "Goddess of Love" Margo Clarke met her match when she tried to find a partner for the wealthy Lainey Belfort. Belfort was a royal pain, but Margo eventually found Australian financier Gabriel Erwood, and the two were wed. What Lainey wasn't aware of was that Gabriel was a man Margo had hired, and was due to divorce her, earn a chunk of her money, and split the take with Margo. But when her partner fell in love with Lainey for real and decided to tell her the truth, Margo took drastic measures to keep him quiet. Margo is the antagonist of the episode "Love Knocked Off". Affably Evil: Margo killed Gabriel after he ruined her moneymaking plan, but she is never less than polite, standing out as one of the consistently kinder inmates to Elsbeth in "Ramen Holiday." Beautiful Singing Voice: While all of the female inmates sing during "Ramen Holiday", it's Margo who Alex notes as having a good voice. Big Beautiful Woman: When Retta plays you, it comes with the territory.

characters.name: CliffMcGrath
characters.description: A former tennis player who couldn't hack it professionally, CliffMcGrathlives out his dreams of play through his son Hunter. When Hunter's dreaded opponent, "Yo-Yo" Arnaldo, left retirement and was soon to face him, Cliff decided to play dirty to secure his son's victory. Lacing a towel with nitroglycerin and positioning it on Yo-Yo's side, Cliff watched as Yo-Yo faltered, glad to see his plan work. Unfortunately, when Yo-Yo collapsed on the court, Cliff discovered his plan had succeeded a littletoowell... Cliff is the antagonist of the episode "Ball Girl". Accidental Murder: Cliff honestly was expecting the nitroglycerin just to throw Yo-Yo off his game, unaware that Yo-Yo's girlfriend had given him other drugs to... erm, "perk him up in the sheets". When the erectile medicine is mixed with the nitroglycerin, presto, one dead tennis player. Cheaters Never Prosper: He sabotaged his son's opponent, and the reveal of this later led his son to get out from under him and likely abandon tennis altogether. Oh yeah, and he'll be going to prison for manslaughter, so that sucks too. Crippling the Competition: Cliff's goal wasn't to kill Johann, but just to throw off his game to allow Hunter the win.

characters.name: Ashlee
characters.description: A ball girl at a tennis court who blackmails coach CliffMcGrath. Or at least, tries to. Ashlee is a minor antagonist of the episode "Ball Girl". Blackmail Backfire: Played with. When she tries to blackmail Cliff for drugging Johann's towel he points outshe's wearing expensive sneakersfrom a bet she made on his underdog son in the match. Rather than be cowed, she just laughs, "Reverse card, nice," and assumes they're now a partnership over Cliff's objections. Didn't Think This Through: Ashlee initially tries to squeeze Cliff to repeat his nitroglycerin trick to help her with her gambling. Cliff explains to her that she's now wearing incredibly expensive sneakers that she got the money for by betting on an underdog player whose opponent died in the middle of a game. So if anything,shewould look a lot likelier as a killer than he does. The Stool Pigeon: As she's being arrested at the end, Ashlee flat-out tells Cliff to his face that she intends to flip on him immediately to get her sentence reduced.

characters.name: Dr. Holmes
characters.description: Vanessa Holmes, one of New York's top plastic surgeons, once had her protégé Astrid Olsen set to join her staff full time. Astrid, however, had other aspirations, and sought to open her own clinic. Vanessa was angered by Astrid's leaving, and angered with Astrid calling out the older guard of plastic surgeons as outdated. Soon enough, that anger boiled over into a vicious attack that left her former mentee dead. Vanessa is the antagonist of the episode "An Ear for an Ear". Casting Gag: A lesbian played by Gina Gershon, eh? Soundsinteresting and familiar... Deadly Doctor: Vanessa is a plastic surgeon who poses as a patient and brutally tortures her former mentee, stabbing her multiple times in the face before killing her. Fake Alibi: She set herself up to appear at a museum by flirting with a security guard. Elsbeth points out that the museum isn't even five minutes away from the clinic, and a group ofclimate change protestorsforces her to try to amend her alibi by buying the same kind of paint they splattered, which has brand exclusivity with all the local hardware stores.

characters.name: Ashton Hayes
characters.description: Ashton Hayes had much to celebrate when his daughter was set to marry Derek Davis, the top accountant at his firm. As Derek was such a trusted employee, Ashton let him onto one of the darker aspects of his business; they made lucrative money scrubbing the funds of shady businessmen and making them look nice and legal. As his soon-to-be-son-in-law, Ashton felt he could trust a man like Derek with such a secret. He was... not correct, and thus ended his daughter's wedding on a sour note by making it look like Derek was the victim of a tragic accident. Ashton is the antagonist of the episode "Something Blue". Affably Evil: Ashton Hayes is a polite, funny man whose worst flaw seems to be perfectionism, and if you don't run afoul of his illegal activities, that is probably the only side of him you'll ever see. Bald of Evil: Ashton's bald as a coot and runs a business as crooked as a dog's hind leg. Chekhov's Skill: Ashton was a cheerleader at Yale. Elsbeth uses this against him when she suggests that he dance with her, which leads to the incriminating evidence falling out of his pocket.

characters.name: Quinn Powers
characters.description: As a young woman, Quinn Powers found herself injured by a mugger whom the police in her town had not warned anyone about. With this injustice angering and driving her, she set out to create Cerberus, an app that allows its users to report crimes and spread the word. It became a success and was soon due for its Initial Public Offering. However, a reporter named Josh Johnson informed Quinn that he planned to report on Cerberus... namely, that it didn't truly work. Not willing to let her work be ruined by the exposé, Quinn decided to concoct a story about a local dognapper to cover Josh's murder, with her bite being much worse than her bark. Quinn is the antagonist of the episode"Artificial Genius". Ambiguously Bi: As seen in"Ramen Holiday", Quinn has attracted the attentions of Alex Modarian, Vanessa Holmes and Joe Dillon in prison. However, she's not seen actively encouraging any of them, so her own orientation remains unclear. Bad Liar: Quinn is so terrible at covering herself that, for once, Elsbeth isn't the only one who can see through her lies easily.Elsbeth: You are very good at not telling the truth. Bad People Abuse Animals: When killing Josh, to maintain the ruse of a dognapper, Quinn kidnaps Josh's dog Gonzo and abandons her in a nearby park, scolding her as she ditches her.

characters.name: Joe Dillon
characters.description: Joe's Bar is an upscale establishment owned by the namesake Joe, a place where one can relax and share their troubles with the friendly bartender. Joe is always there to help his clients, who are as close to him as family. Particularly close to him is Ivy Benson, and her latest visit to the bar brought bad news. She had just lost a chance at a well-paying position due to a social media post about her former college roommate, Gemma Nelson, who had tormented her so much that she ended up dropping out. Joe, always supportive of Ivy, decided that when she left town for a visit to her sister, he would make his way to Gemma's apartment to confront her about everything she had done to Ivy... or so he thought at the time. Joe is the antagonist of the episode "Sweet Justice". Ax-Crazy: Joe didn't seem to have too much of a problem strangling a woman to death on behalf of one of his customers. Bartender Confidant: A dark twist. Joe isLoved by Allof his bar patrons for his willingness to listen to (and solve) their problems. This is why he tries to kill the former bully of his crush, Ivy Benson, after she tells him that she messed up an interview after being reminded of her. The Bus Came Back: He comes back inThe Cameoin "Ramen Holiday" after beingPut on a Prison Bus, leering at Elsbeth through the prison bars.

characters.name: Nadine Clay
characters.description: Model Nadine Clay turned heads in the fashion world when she announced she would be making her final run at the latest show of Nick Garrison. Part of that was due to the fact that Garrison was her soon-to-be-ex-husband for his womanizing ways, and the divorce as a result, acrimonious to say the least. The show ended on a low note when the body of photographer Ezra Tate was found in the media pit, shot in the back during the spectacle. Elsbeth soon discovered Nadine had a particular motive for doing him in, in the form of something known as "The Pangaea Project"... Except, as it was discovered, she in fact wasn't Ezra's killer in the end. Nadine appears to be the antagonist of the episode "A Fitting Finale", but that is ultimately proven wrong. Big Eater: Now that she's finished modeling, she's making a point of enjoying the junk food she denied herself for years and is often seen eating in her scenes. However, she has abandoned this by the time of "Elsbeth Flips the Bird", as she gained a pound. Blackface: In her days at art school, she and Ezra took their assignment on fashion in different culture by having herself made up in all sorts of way. This of course meant doing basically all the color-faces, with Matteo describing each one as more offensive than the last. Understandably, Ezra chose to blackmail her with this, as her name would be mud if the photos were released.

characters.name: The Killer at the Fashion Show
characters.description: The illustrious fashion designer Matteo Hart was once upon a time the teacher to model Nadine Clay, designer Nick Garrison, and photographer Ezra Tate. Matteo is the true antagonist of the episode "A Fitting Finale". Affably Evil: Matteo is genuinely kind to Elsbeth, sees her, and values her. He's also a double murderer (the first murder was justified, the second was not). Killing in Self-Defense: His killing of Bobby Domingo was a justified murder in the effort of saving one of his former students/friends. The same can not be said for his killing of Ezra (the student/friend in question). Legacy Seeker: Matteo murdered Bobby Domingo and Ezra because of his obsession with preserving his legacy.

characters.name: Phillip Cross
characters.description: With a love of the opera stemming from a young age, ex-lawyer Phillip Cross naturally got himself a subscription to the Thursday Series. Phillip often found himself sitting behind an older woman until her passing. With her death, her grandson Eddie Reese inherited her subscription, and quickly proved himself to have no true culture whatsoever, using his position only to woo women. With one theater rule too many broken, Phillip snapped and took it upon himself to permanently end Eddie's subscription. Phillip is the antagonist of the episode "Subscription to Murder". Actor Allusion: As he did inThe Good Fight,Nathan Laneplays another lawyer. This time, though, he is the murderer. Affably Evil: Phillip is a murderer but he's got Nathan Lane's charm and impeccable manners and a genuine love and appreciation for the arts. Amoral Attorney: Philip is a retired attorney who was forced out due to being overly argumentative, and he ultimately murdered Eddie for petty reasons.

characters.name: Neal Dorsey
characters.description: Making his billions in the paint industry, Neal Dorsey went alongside his son Neal Jr. (Randy, as he prefers to be called) to a space training camp alongside fellow billionaires to go into the cosmos. Unfortunately, one of the fellow "astronauts" was green energy billionaire Gavin Morrissey, whom Randy worshipped and who constantly teased him with the nickname "Snoozer." Being trapped in close proximity to the man finally caused Neal to harm his rival lethally. Neal is the antagonist of the episode "The Wrong Stuff". Berserk Button: Being called "Snoozer" can put him in a sour mood real quick. Big Bad: Of the episode "The Wrong Stuff." Boring, but Practical: His stance on his career. Paint may not be as exciting as green energy or getting him millions of social media followers, but it's practical, reliable, and simple, to say nothing of netting him billions.

characters.name: Mac Altman
characters.description: Mackenzie is a flightyFormer Child Starwho murdered her trainer and good friend, Sonny Miller. She wakes up the following day with no memory of what happened and relies on Elsbeth to help her discover what happened. While Mac is technically the killer of the episode "Devil's Night", she is not the antagonist. Catchphrase: Mac is as embarrassed as anyone to hear that during a drunken rant, she repeated her oldFather's Keeperscharacter Sam's catchphrase of "I'll be the judge of that!" Forced into Evil: Mac didn't mean to kill Sonny, but she was drugged by Danny into doing it. Former Child Star: Mac went from a child sitcom star to a tabloid-fodder mess.

characters.name: The "Devil's Night" Killer
characters.description: Manager and lawyer to the former child star Mac Altman, Danny had a sweet thing going. His naïve client was a gold mine for him to steal money from her supposed "investments". Unfortunately for him, one of Mac's "buddies", drug dealer turned rapper Sonny Miller, found out he was stealing her money and wanted in on it. Danny took it upon himself to follow Mac on Halloween night and slip her a hypnotic drug in order to use her to give Sonny one hell of a trick. Danny is the antagonist of the episode "Devil's Night". Amoral Attorney: Daniel has been stealing millions of dollars from Mac, used her to kill his blackmailer, and set her up to get them off. Amoral Talent Agent: In a crossover withAmoral Attorney, Danny is revealed to be Mac's manager as well as her lawyer. He was stealing money from her (and the previous client he managed) and set Mac up to kill Sonny because Sonny was blackmailing him. Big Bad: Of "Devil's Night."

characters.name: Roselyn Bridwell
characters.description: For years, Roselyn Bridwell has been a client of the exclusive jewelry store Vivienne's. However, a changing of the guard resulted in her finding out that such loyalty and frequent shopping had left her very close to going flat broke. For her, this proved to be an insult, and to that end, she decided she'd get herself payback by robbing the store of valuable stones. However, when her efforts to recruit an employee resulted in nearly blowing the lid off the job, she attempted to solve the issue with a spoonful of poison. Roselyn is the antagonist of the episode "Diamonds Are for Elsbeth". Casting Gag:Vanessa Williamsplays a superficial woman and a TV show antagonist obsessed with material things (in this case, jewelry), just like her magazine editor character Wilhelmina Slater inUgly Betty. Mock Millionaire: Her frequent jewelry buys have left her with her trust fund almost drained. Never My Fault: Roselyn believes that she is blameless in her financial problems despite the fact that she's the one who bought so much expensive jewelry in the first place. When she first learn just how little money she has left, she gets snippy over her accountant saying her spending habits have left her near broke, while she sits in a room full of jewelry she doesn't really need.

characters.name: The Heist Group
characters.description: To aid her heist, Roselyn Bridwell enlists her friend Celeste, the owner of the recently-bankrupt Two Scoops frozen yogurt chain; Judith, a longtime Vivienne's employee who is being unceremoniously laid off; and Hugo, a forger who can swap out Vivenne's jewels with fakes. The three are minor antagonists of the episode "Diamonds Are for Elsbeth". The Bad Guy Wins: Though the heist fails, Judith is last seen living it up in Paris, having stolen all of Roselyn's jewelry. Karma Houdini: Judith cuts a deal with the D.A. to avoid jail time and gets no trouble for robbing Roselyn blind. Never My Fault: Celeste blames Big Pharma for her frozen yogurt business going bust.

characters.name: Chef Veev
characters.description: Genevieve Hale is chef and restaurateur at one of the city's most in-demand restaurants, and is on the verge of a huge hotel deal. Unfortunately one of her employees, dissatisfied with his own position, has started undermining her. She chokes him to death in a rage and pretends that an outsider was responsible for attacking them both. Chef Veev is the antagonist of the episode "Elsbeth Flips the Bird". Angry Chef: Veev clearly has severe anger issues, to the point where she delivers aNo-Holds-Barred Beatdownto Jordan...and thenhasto kill him. Berserk Button: Veev could take Jordan trying to ruin her business. But insulting her lamb shanks drives her to attack him. Corrupted Character Copy: AGender Flipof Carmy inThe Bear (2022).Both are intense, obsessive chefs taught by abusive mentors who become restaurant owners and struggle in their position. However, Veev is a murderer.

characters.name: DeeDeeDashers
characters.description: DeeDeeis a Christmas lifestyle influencer with her husband Dirk. DeeDeeis the antagonist of the episode "Gold, Frankincense, and Murder." Alliterative Name: Lampshaded by her husband (see below). Bad Influencer:DeeDeeis a Christmas-themed influencer who, instead of turning her husband in when she figured out he planned to kill her, killedhiminstead and simply used his death in an effort to pivot away from the Christmas theme shehated. Conviction by Contradiction: Elsbeth catchesDeeDeeby noticing that her business plan with monochromatic colors was actually dated from monthsbeforeDirk died.

characters.name: Regina Coburn
characters.description: One of the main stars of the long-running crime proceduralFather Crime, Regina is an actress with her eyes set on doingMacb- well,The Scottish Play, especially since she has become sick to death of the show she's most known for. Unfortunately, showrunner Cal Reed had other plans for her career, and with the show's grueling production schedule, she wouldn't be able to leave. Not until she did something... Shakespearean about it. Regina is the antagonist of the episode "Toil and Trouble." All for Nothing: Wanted to star inMacbethso she could be taken seriously as an actress, but her Scottish accent is so awful that even if she'd gotten away with Cal's murder, she'd have become a laughingstock. Bad "Bad Acting":Zig Zagged. Regina is shown to be a decent actress (at least relative to her performance in a low-rentPolice Procedural), but she ishorribleat accents. Convenient Coma: In-universe; Regina wants to bePut on a BusinFather Crimeso that she can doMacbeth.

characters.name: Tom Murphy
characters.description: Tom owns and runs the Heiwa Zen spa, catered to the rich and famous, where he engages in controlling behavior and extreme treatments. He is the antagonist of "Unalive and Well." Be as Unhelpful as Possible: TheBeware the Nice Onesvariation. Tom is very helpful and open with the police, telling them about Cole/Billy and his sister, to disguise his real murder of Billy. Foreign Culture Fetish: Tom is a white man who nevertheless runs a spa that is themed around a vague combination of "eastern" religion and homeopathy. Hapless Self-Help: Tom runs a Heiwa Zen spa that talks to a big game about healing, while committing a cold-blooded murder after Cole/Billy catches him out and proves that Tom was violating his agreement with Cole/Billy's family.

characters.name: Peter Hepson
characters.description: Peter is the identical twin of Bill Hepson and co-founder of Hepson Capital. He is the antagonist of "Finance Bros". All Psychology Is Freudian: Despite dismissing "that Freud crap," Peter is clearly very affected when Elsbeth brings up his and Bill's mother. Cain and Abel: Peter has always been resentful of their mother's favoritism to Bill. This becomes worse when Bill gains a generous reputation and threatens Peter's reputation as well as Hepson Capital's. Green-Eyed Monster: Part of why he wanted to kill Bill*Shaddup,you.is because the latter has always been seen as the favorite, be it from their mother or the public eye. Bill getting a boost in popularity for denouncing his wealth tips the scales.

characters.name: The "Tiny Town" Killer
characters.description: Howard is the antagonist of the episode "Tiny Town." The Heavy: Implied. Howard says that theCEOspaid him to kill Hayley and George, but he's still the biggest threat of the story and is willing to kill Elsbeth when he realizes she's rumbled him. Meaningful Name: In an episode paying a sort of homage toRear Window, it's fitting that Howard's last name is the same as the murderer in that movie. Never One Murder: Kills both Hayley and George in the same way. Only in It for the Money: Howard says that the company'sCEOspaid him to murder Hayley and George.

characters.name: Lawrence Grey
characters.description: Lawrence runs Outmatch Education Consulting, which grooms his wealthy clients' children from a young age to get into elite schools. However, one of his success stories, Ethan Brooks, who became director of admissions at Baden University, grew resentful of Lawrence for how his life turned out and sought revenge by rejecting all of Outmatch's clients. To save his business, Lawrence decides to reject Ethan's application...to life. Lawrence is the antagonist of the episode "Foiled Again". Academia Elitism: Lawrence has made it his business to get his clients into Ivy League schools, manipulating Ethan Brooks out of his drama school dreams years ago, and responds with condescension when Elsbeth tells him she sent Teddy to a non-elite school as a Philosophy major. Bad People Abuse Animals: After Lawrence lies to the police about his pet cat Veritas having died long ago in order to cover up his murder, the next scene shows him looming over Veritas declaring that he's "got to go". He then tells his daughter that Veritas died when she returns home and shows her his urn.Subverted, thankfully, when it turns out that he only took him to a shelter. The Cobbler's Children Have No Shoes: While he makes money off of rich parents who want to strong-arm their kids into resembling Ivy League success stories, his own daughter, Mandy, is taking a "nineteen-month" gap year in a Hiking and Creativity program.

characters.name: Chloe
characters.description: Chloe. A beautiful, elegant, and intelligent lady of the- er, no,consultantoften seen on the arms of New York's wealthiest citizens. The one she most often saw was real estate billionaire Nathan Jordan. Chloe is the antagonist of the episode "Tearjerker". Affably Evil: Chloe is a murderer who frames two innocent people for her crimes but she's very charming and polite with no indication that her friendliness is a cover, genuinely liking Elsbeth and Elsbeth feeling the same, being regretful that she has to take Chloe in and even offering to set her up with a good defense attorney. She even admits she would have liked to have been her friend if things were different and takes her arrest gracefully, only asking that the painting Nathan gifted her be given to a museum so everyone can enjoy it. Even the "evil" part is debatable as she only killed Nathan because he wanted to die and she genuinely loved him and was saddened by his decision, with the only really immoral part of the equation being framing Deborah and Dr Yamamoto per Nathan's wishes. Badass Cape: Chloeswishesout of the apartment after killing Nathan Jordan. But Not Too Bi: Discussed. She says she is happy towork withElsbeth, as she has exclusively male clients and hasn't worked with a woman for years.

characters.name: Pupetta Del Ponte
characters.description: Pupetta is the antagonist of the episode "Scenes From an Italian Restaurant". Bad "Bad Acting": Part of what gets Elsbeth to first suspect her is when she arrives on the scene of Gene's hit-and-run wearing black like she was at a funeral, carrying a Bible, and laying the emotions onreallythick. Crime of Passion: She killed Goldie in a fit of rage when he refused to accept that he was the father of her baby. Femme Fatale: As both a teenager and a young woman, Pupetta is a beautiful,Hot-Bloodedmafia princess who murdered her ex-lover, Goldie, and continues to manipulate Gene Sr, who she knows adores her. She also tells Fleming that she knows he "loved hunting her." Femme Fatalons: As a young woman, she had very long French tips. Elsbeth sees one of them missing in a moviebased onthe crime, and she realizes that theFemme FatalePupetta used them to scratch Goldie just before she killed him in a fit of passion, and that'swhat solves the crime.

characters.name: Marilyn Gladwell
characters.description: Marilyn Gladwell is a psychic whose wealthy clientele includes Phyllis Pierson, whom Marilyn is persuading to sell her late husband's snack food company to a competing business. Phyllis' stepson Tim won't have it, however, suspecting that Marilyn is up to something. So Marilyn decides to take control of her future... by ending Tim's. Marilyn is the antagonist of the episode "I See... Murder". Con Artist: On top of the typical high prices for a psychic, she's trying to manipulate Phyllis into selling her company to their rival because she is an investor in the latter and would stand to make a mint off the sale. Fake Alibi: Marilyn claims to have given a phone reading the night Tim was murdered, but her assistant Reagan admits it was her. Fauxreigner: Marilyn turns out to be from a small Pennsylvania town and makes up her story of being from Europe to get more clients.

characters.name: Freya Frostad
characters.description: Known as a guru of decluttering, Freya Frostad prides herself on her method of only keeping 44 items at a time. Unfortunately, there still grew clutter in her marriage when things turned polyamorous. She grew much more attached to Taylor, their third, and decided she could remove some of that clutter taking her husband out of the picture. Freya is the antagonist of the episode "Hot Tub Crime Machine". All for Nothing: Freya murdered Axel so she could have Taylor all to herself, but almost immediately afterwards, Taylor wants to break up with her because she only wants to be in a throuple, forcing her to find another partner anyway to avoid losing her completely. Alliterative Name:FreyaFrostad. Bad "Bad Acting": Freya is seen acting in one of Alex's plays in "Ramen Holiday." Her performance isn't great.

characters.name: Arthur Greene Jr.
characters.description: The owner of Arthur Greene and Sons Funeral Home, known for serving New York's elite while maintaining strict privacy, Arthur takes great pride in his work. That's why he gets rattled when his "Alternative Thinker" nephew, Russell, starts asking questions about the recent funeral of a famous author, believing that she faked her death and their family is complicit in it. When Russell makes it clear he won't let the matter rest, Arthur decides to do whatever he can to keep the truth buried. Literally. Arthur is the antagonist of "Four Body Problem". Creepy Mortician: Arthur is the murderous owner of a funeral home, but he is otherwiseaffableexcept when he murders his own nephew and desperately tries to cover it up, which causes him to be unprofessional. Extremely Protective Child: Exaggerated. He killed his own nephew, Russell, for asking around about N.D. Longacre's death—because his father was in the early stages of dementia when he accidentally switched Longacre's ashes with those of Polly, his beloved dog. Arthur was determined to cover up thatTragic Mistake, to murderous levels. Murder in the Family: He kills his own nephew just for snooping around asking questions.

characters.name: The Surprise "I Know What You Did Thirty-Three Summers Ago" Killer
characters.description: While not an antagonist, Delia becomes a murderer in the episode "I Know What You Did Thirty-Three Summers Ago." For the main antagonist of this episode, see Judge Crawford's folder in the main characters section. Big Beautiful Woman: She's a broader woman, and it does not take away her loveliness. Convicted by Public Opinion: Despite being acquitted of Andy's murder, people still view Delia as a killer. She's unable to get a job and is living with her brother. Whatever was left of her good reputation dies permanently when she guns Crawford down. Heroic Sacrifice: Delia knows full well she'll go to prison for killing Crawford, but goes through with it to ensure he doesn't get away with his crimes. Sympathetic Murderer: Considering Crawford nearly had her sent to prison for her boyfriend's murder, essentially ruined her life with his frame job and her trial, and used every connection he had to evade justice at every turn, it certainly isn't hard to see why she figured that gunning him down looked like a good option.

characters.name: Rod Bedford
characters.description: A man with far more money than he knows what to do with can find himself facing an odd problem: boredom. That was Rod Bedford's dilemma, which is why he turned to a bucket list of crazy stunts and activities to try and get a thrill out of his life. Yet, no matter what he tried, nothing provided the right spark. That all changed when he nearly shot his friend by accident at their exclusive club. Once he felt the thrill in his system, he added something peculiar to his bucket list: "kill a human being", and later, "get away with murder." Rod is the antagonist of the episode "I've Got a Little List". Blatant Lies: When his friend says that he's "sure [Rod] feels awful", he unconvincingly replies "...yes." For the Evulz: Lampshaded by Elsbeth when she says that Rod is trying to "feel something" through murder. Hate Sink: Rod, the sociopathic little prick, makes himself look unlikable complaining about his bucket list no one else could afford to complete, and gets worse from there when he murders a man in cold blood.

characters.name: The Prison Killer
characters.description: The warden of the Midtown Correctional Facility. Mama Martin is the antagonist of "Ramen Holiday". Failed a Spot Check: Didn't realize the ramen knife she confiscated from Chef Veev had not been properly cleaned, so her signature blend of herbs caught Elsbeth's attention. Wardens Are Evil:Zig-Zagged. She doesn't appear to be this at first, as while she tries to be intimidating she also allows the inmates a surprising amount of freedom and is friendly to Elsbeth. However, this turns out to be because she is extorting money from the wealthy prisoners through Alex Modarian so they can access goods from the outside. Once he decides to rat out her scheme to his own advantage, she kills him. Wolf in Sheep's Clothing: She spends much of her episode, which is not in theReverse Whodunnitformat, appearing to be an ally to Elsbeth, even letting her have access to her stash of Lean Cuisine.

characters.name: Laurel Hammond-Muntz
characters.description: The head writer onWay Late with Scotty Bristol. Laurel is a long-suffering professional who’s endured years of Scotty's egotism and abuse. Not only does Scotty callously shred the jokes pitched by his writing staff, but he publicly humiliates Laurel’s husband, Mickey, on nearly every episode. The relentless ridicule takes a toll on Mickey’s fragile health, further straining his already weak heart. When Scotty refuses to give Mickey the time and rest he desperately needs, Laurel decides that enough is enough — and that it's time for Scotty to make his final exit... stage left. Laurel is the antagonist of "Yes, and...?". Black Widow: Downplayed. Laurel first seduces Scotty, using their years of intimacy and his general lecherousness to put him in a vulnerable enough position to strangle him with his own tie through the shredder. Then she indirectly kills Mickey by causing his heart attack, though this was not her intention. Love Makes You Evil: Laurel kills Scotty in part because of how cruel he was to her husband Mickey. Downplayed when her cover-up ends up killing Mickey and she pins Scotty's murder on him. Underestimating Badassery: Downplayed. Laurel kills Scotty because she thinks it's the only way for her put-upon husband to be free of his abuse and take care of himself. Mickey is the one to find the body because he was on his way up to finally give an ultimatum to Scotty to either give him time off or quit. Had Laurel trusted Mickey and not jumped to murder, things would have worked out better for the Muntzes and Scotty.

characters.name: Nolan Hurst
characters.description: Nolan Hurst is a former trader who went to prison for insider trading for four years before getting out. In that time, his relationship with his young daughter became strained, and he aimed to fix it by getting her a particular doll she once asked for. He turned to Patrick Palmer, manager of Becker's Toys flagship branch, even being willing to pay over ten times the doll's worth to get it. But Patrick, being the un-scrupled sort, tried to get the money and give him the wrong doll. Everything went downhill when Nolan killed Patrick in a scuffle and tried to get the doll he truly wanted from the store, only for Elsbeth to arrive and quickly peg him as the killer. Desperate to not go back to jail, Nolan grabbed an officer's gun, hoping all the hostage movies he saw in the joint will let him get away. Nolan is the antagonist of "Doll Day Afternoon". Didn't Think This Through: Nolan assumed his daughter would still want a Spirited Girl Doll after three years and paid 15 times the market price on it. Engineered Public Confession: A rare example where it's meant to help the one confessing. Elsbeth uses the nanny cam the cops are using to look into the store to get Nolan to open up about Patrick's death, revealing that Patrick was trying to scam him out of all he had left, and that the murder was both an accident and had nothing to do with drug smuggling as Captain Tully had initially thought. Genre Savvy: He watched a lot of crime and hostage movies in prison and references these to create his own hostage plan. He didn't plan on Elsbeth.

characters.name: Raquel Drawboski
characters.description: Raquel is a self-styled grief influencer who built an empire on widowhood after a “tragic accident” supposedly claimed her husband eighteen months ago. Now she headlines the hit reality seriesBlack Veil, where she’s meant to choose a new lover to “move on.” But when her very-much-alive husband resurfaces—threatening her brand, her contracts, and the story millions have bought — Raquel realizes the truth would annihilate her image. To protect her fame, she ensures his second chance at life is devastatingly brief. Raquel is the antagonist of "Good Grief" Ambition Is Evil: Played with. Was Raquel wrong for wanting a better life? Not entirely. Was she wrong to exploit the death of her high school sweetheart over it? Probably. Was she wrong to kill him? Definitely. Bad "Bad Acting": Once we see Raquel onBlack Veil, it's clear that however real her grief over losing Johnny was when it actually happened, her grief now is as phony as a three dollar bill. Kaya even mentions that whenever she watchedBlack Veil, it always seemed Raquel was laying it on thick. Bad Influencer: A "grief influencer" who is willing to murder her husband she had grieved so much over because she didn't want to lose all the wealth her platform had given her. Even when Johnny's infidelity comes out, she manages to pivot to a "betrayal influencer".

characters.name: Sharon Norman
characters.description: Sharon is a Sleepy Hollow suburban housewife who runs multiple neighborhood organizations and loves being in control. This is challenged by her free-spirited rival neighbor Beryl for three years, until she decides to use the annual Sleepy Hollow Halloween celebrations to kill Beryl. Sharon is the primary antagonist of "Ick, A Bod". Control Freak: Her first act as Beryl's neighbor is to give her a set of neighborhood "guidelines". She has rules for what kids eat, how to run neighborhood meetings, noise ordinances, etc. She also hates not knowing what her family is doing. Everyone around her, even her husband, are put off by how controlling she is. Cranky Neighbor: To Beryl. She disapproves of the woman's rebellious spirit from the moment they meet, hates her wind chimes, her parties, her habits, the company she keeps, everything about her. Doubles withNosy Neighborsince she constantly spied on Beryl. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: Sharon is protective of daughter Avery, andacts quickly to squash things when it sounds like Elsbeth and Donnelly consider Avery a suspect. Elsbeth subtly plays on this feeling to get Sharon off guard.

characters.name: The Second "Ick, A Bod" Killer
characters.description: For months, anesthesiologist Lucas Norman bore witness to his wife Sharon's feud with their new neighbor Beryl Nix, The two women had vastly different personality differences, one of their biggest being their feelings towards the big tree in Sharon and Lucas' yard, the Towering Maple. Beryl wished it gone to have a better view while Sharon considered it a sacred part of the Norman family. It occurred to Lucas that maybe if the Maple was dead, it would have to be cut down, and with it gone, his wife and neighbor could bury their rivalry. Oh, how wrong he was. Lucas is the secondary killer (though not quite the antagonist) of "Ick, A Bod". Didn't Think This Through: Lucas figured if the Towering Maple was no more, Sharon and Beryl might have been able to put the past behind them and maybe start to be friends. It didn't seem to cross his mind that Sharon would believe Beryl herself killed the tree and take it out on her. No one would blame him for not considering Sharon would jump to cutting Beryl's head off, but one would think being married to her would give him some insight on how she'd take the tree's death. Gone Horribly Wrong: His efforts to get Sharon and Beryl to like each other resulted in the latter's grisly murder at the former's hands and the former going to prison. Not Distracted by the Sexy: Beryl painting topless in her house (visible from the windows) didn't stir much in him. In his words, as an anesthesiologist, he sees plenty of people without their clothes on.

characters.name: Gary Pidgeon
characters.description: Gary Pidgeon is the founder of the Pidgeon Print, a prominent poetry journal that has recently fallen into dire financial straits. His "friend" Delores Feinn, a cantankerous longtime supporter of the journal (and also a horrible poet) has promised to bequeath a substantial sum upon her death, but is about to take her business to a rival journal. With bankruptcy looming and no other options in sight, Gary decides to expedite matters and go from writing poems to writing Delores's obituary... Gary is the antagonist of "Poetic Justice" All for Nothing: Gary killed Delores because he believed that doing so would earn the Pidgeon Print a generous amount of money from her will, only to find out from her lawyer that Delores was nowhere near as rich as he believed, and only left Gary's business less than 500 dollars. Black and Nerdy: Gary is Black, and also a poet who wears tweed jackets and runs a poetry journal. Motive Rant: When confronted by Elsbeth, goes into a tirade about how Delores strung him along, leading to the confession that seals his fate.

characters.name: Craig Harris
characters.description: The high-strung CEO ofFinTech, Craig lives in a world where every headline reads like a personal death threat. Obsessed with the rising “Eat the Rich” rhetoric, he’s transformed part of his mansion into a state-of-the-art riot retreat—a bunker built not just for safety, but for the kind of doomsday fantasies only the ultra-wealthy can afford. When he discovers that his crisis manager, Anders Wittman, is planning to resign, Craig’s paranoia spikes into something volatile and radioactive. In his panicked mind, Anders isn’t just quitting—he’s turning traitor. And so Craig repurposes his panic room, converting it from a fortress of protection into a chamber with a far deadlier function. Craig is the antagonist of "Bunker Down". Addled Addict: He says that his thinking Anders was out to ruin him "isn't the ketamine talking". Misanthrope Supreme: Craig has nothing but disdain for humans, preferring AI instead. The Paranoiac: He is convinced near everyone in the world is out to get him.

characters.name: The Driver
characters.description: An unfortunate citizen who cut the freedom of imprisoned fixer Anders Wittman tragically short after he managed to escape the secure bunker of his client Craig Harris. While by no means an antagonist, the driver is technically the killer of "Bunker Down". Ambiguous Gender: Officer Reynolds only calls them "the driver". Accidental Murder: They ran over Anders because he came out of a manhole in a way that gave them no time to stop. Flat Character: They are the murderer that the audience is told the least about, mostly because they aren't really a character, all things considered.

characters.name: Mother Constance
characters.description: Mother Constance is the strict Mother Superior of the Convent of Our Lady of Grace and Mercy, who has devoted her life to leading and protecting her order. So when hard times cause the convent to be sold out from under her to blasphemous pop icon Alaïa Jade—threatening to turn the sisters from the only home they've ever known—Constance’s world buckles. Faced with the ruin of everything she holds sacred, she resorts to measures that violate her vows, rattle her conscience and may be the gravest sin of her life... Mother Constance is the antagonist of "And Then There Were Nuns". All for Nothing: Not only does murdering Alaïa fail to prevent the convent from being sold, but Elsbeth getting it saved as a historic landmark means that Constance has taken a young life and got herself jailed for murder when she wouldn't have had to. Alliterative Name:ConstanceCabot. Blatant Lies: Claims to have accepted Alaïa's purchase of the convent for the good of the church, but Sister Frances later contradicts this. Constance also says she forbade Alaïa to enter the bell tower, which upset her. Elsbeth shows Constance a picture of them where Alaïa doesn't look upset at all, which Constance claims is due to the camera angle. While not the biggest liar Elsbeth's encountered, as Elsbeth emphasizes duringThe Summation, breaking the eighth commandment is a big taboo for a nun.

characters.name: Sister Darby
characters.description: Sister Darby is a nun at the Convent of Our Lady of Grace and Mercy who was always getting in trouble with Mother Constance, mainly for her mistimed bell ringing. The day pop star Alaïa Jade went on a walkthrough after purchasing the convent, Darby put extra effort into ringing the bells at the right time, not knowing her timing was way off... or who was in the bell tower. While by no means an antagonist, Sister Darby is technically the killer of "And Then There Were Nuns". The Dog Bites Back: After facing the worst of Mother Constance's scolding and discipline, plus being tricked into killing Alaïa Jade, she finally gets one up on Constance in the end by challenging her to swear her innocence to God, which Constance cannot do, andusing her own words against her. My God, What Have I Done?: Bursts into tears when realizing her ringing the bell killed Alaïa. Unwitting Pawn: Constance uses her as such in Alaïa's murder.

characters.name: Peyton Ramsey
characters.description: Peyton is the much younger girlfriend of Russell Willoughby, who had come out of retirement to coach the St. Ivan's University basketball team. Peyton was criticized for her outspokenness and marriage to Willoughby, especially by the college's athletic director Dave Coppins who blamed her for the team's decline. Shortly afterward Coppins turned up dead, and Peyton initially seemed like the killer, but she turned out to have an alibi. Peyton appears to be the antagonist of the episode "Basket Case", but it turns out to be otherwise. Jerkass Has a Point: Always tells it like it is, if rather bluntly. May–December Romance: She dates Coach Willoughby, who's old enough to be her grandfather, and she ends up dating senator Lindsey Graham*The episode aired months before Graham's death in 2026, so just roll with it.. For sake of reference, Lana Condor was 28 when the episode was aired, SamMcMurraywas 73, and Graham was 70. No Celebrities Were Harmed: Based on Jordon Hudson, the much-younger girlfriend of football coach Bill Belichick, who was rumored to have been banned from the training facilities (unlike Peyton, Hudson's case was a false rumor).

characters.name: The "Basket Case" Killer
characters.description: A basketball coach from the pros who came out of retirement to coach a college team, and who kills athletic director Dave Coppins out of anger at what he heard Coppins saying to girlfriend Peyton Ramsey on his listening devices. Coach Willoughby is the antagonist of "Basket Case". Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He appears meek and somewhat hapless most of the time. However, he kills Coppins in a fit of rage. After that, he's good at covering his tracks by doing things like marrying Peyton—thus covering himself with spousal privilege—after she sees the incriminating concealer on his hands. He also tries to frame one of his players. No Celebrities Were Harmed: Based on former New England Patriots and current North Carolina Tar Heels football coach Bill Belichick. Sinister Surveillance: He previously got in trouble for bugging an opposing team (an incident known as "Tapegate") and is now bugging his own team.

characters.name: Tiff Giles
characters.description: Tiff Giles was once modeling royalty—the "It girl" of the legendary Glamazons—until a brutal attack ended her career and left her slinging drinks at a Chester, Pennsylvania dive bar. Years later, her former roommate Madison, now a thriving businesswoman, extends an olive branch: a reunion photoshoot to recapture their glory days. Tiff wants nothing to do with her old life—until she discovers that Madison and her sleazy husband TJ orchestrated the very attack that destroyed her. Suddenly, the photoshoot becomes more than a comeback opportunity. It's the perfect stage for revenge. Tiff is the antagonist of "Glamazons" Career-Ending Injury: In this case, a scarred face and lost eye from an attack caused by Madison and her husband TJ. Eye Scream: The attack orchestrated on her caused the CD she was listening to to pop out of its player, break, and slash out her left eye. The fact that she was left alone for hours likely didn't help. Failed a Spot Check: Did a good job wiping off the fingerprints,except for the foil from the wine bottle, which she pocketed asbartenders tend to do, which gets her caught.

characters.name: Harris Monroe
characters.description: Harris Monroe is a former ballet dancer who now focuses on his young daughter Noelle's dance career. When an avant garde director is hired to do a revisionist version ofThe Nutcrackerwith no children in the cast, he decides to go to extremes to make sure Noelle gets her shot at Clara. Harris is the antagonist of "A Hard Nut to Crack". The Bad Guy Wins: Harris is ultimately caught and sent to prison, but he gets exactly what he wanted as Noelle still gets to play Clara, presumably because Elsbeth doesn't want to punish the daughter for the father's crimes. He even convinces the police to allow him to watch her perform before he is taken away. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: He clearly loves his daughter and getting her her dream role motivates him murdering Donovan. Fake Alibi: Books a physical therapy appointment close to the Midtown Ballet demonstration, knowing the clinic, which operates on a sliding scale basis, is notoriously slow, allowing him to sneak out to commit the murder and head back before being caught. Elsbeth finds it suspicious that someone who married into money would attend such a clinic.

characters.name: Archer Kopunek
characters.description: Aging is an inevitable process. Or, at least it is for those that aren't wealthy "biohackers" like Archer. Having squandered some of his health in his earlier years, he drove himself to live as perfectly healthy as he could. Things turned even better when he came across a young man who practically won the genetic lottery. But when that young man decided that he wanted to leave and truly experience life, Archer decided that death could come for the young man at least, especially when he could increase his own life span in return. Archer is the antagonist of "Ol' Man Liver". Billy Needs an Organ: Downplayed. Archer doesn't actuallyneeda new liver; the one from his son works fine, and Archer is not terminally ill. But since it isn't working well enough for Archer's longevity goals and his plasma donor, Tyler, is about to leave him, he goes to crazy lengths to secure his own longevity. Fake Alibi: He switches his and Tyler's fitness rings, then while Tyler is sound asleep gives himself a rapid heart rate just before the software is set to update, alerting the hospital. Then, when the update is in progress, he goes to Tyler's room, injects him in time for the approaching ambulance to harvest his organs, switches the rings, and gets back in bed in time for the software to turn back on. It's exposed because Archer's ring registered a much lower cellular age than Tyler's at the time. Immortality Immorality: Commits murder in his pursuit of eternal youth.

characters.name: Felix West
characters.description: Wig-making in New York City is a small world. Only five people in the city are considered the cream of the crop, and the bottom rung of that ladder is Felix "The Rug Doctor" West, so called because he's stuck making toupees for wealthy businessmen and hospital patients while his colleagues serve performers and socialites. That is, until daytime host Lina Vyanti walks through his door and tells him she wants to defect from her current wigmaker, Domenico Cappelli. But to match her Molten-Gold hair color during a shortage, Felix resorts to drastic measures, and only lowers himself further once Domenico gets wind of the betrayal. Felix is the antagonist of "All's Hair". All for Nothing: Felix accepts Lina Vyanti's offer in hopes of landing more glamorous clientele, but when she finds out how he obtained the hair for her wig, she turns him down. Plus he'll now go to jail for murder. Ambiguously Gay: Mentions that he got in trouble for playing with his sister's Barbie dolls. Ambition Is Evil: He is so pumped with the idea of his wigs being more upscale than wigs for ill people and toupees for businessmen, he ends up betraying one of his rivals, stealing hair off of a teen girl and then murdering said rival for finding out.

characters.name: Simon Carroll
characters.description: Cruciverbalist. Faultfinder. Pianist. These are just a few words to describe Simon Carroll, a piano tuner and crossword enthusiast who has shown unwavering loyalty to the Metropolitan Tribune's crossword puzzles. He's so committed, in fact, that every year, without fail, Simon participates in the paper's annual crossword competition. This year is different for two reasons: the woman he cares about, divorcee ElaineMcClusk, and the object of his ire, crossword editor and competition head Morris Long. Simon had already been losing patience with the editor for letting modern slang and references sneak into the puzzles, but asking Elaine out was a step too far. When his complaints resulted in Morris throwing him out of the competition, Simon found the best solution to be an eight-letter word for taking a human life... Simon is the antagonist of "Murder Six Across". Alas, Poor Villain: Even with all he's done, it's not hard to feel bad for him when he's forced to miss the finals and Elaine ultimately rejects him for being a murderer, having already realized she loved Morris precisely because Simon killed him. All for Nothing: Simon kills Morris for barring him from the tournament and threatening his chance with Elaine... and this causes him to be pulled away from the finals and having Elaine reject him for what he did. Creature of Habit: The thing that does him in. The fact that hehasto do theMetropolitan Tribunecrossword everyday, and has since he was young, plus his tendency to always carry change, is what gets him caught at the train station near where the body was found (see below).

characters.name: Izzy Langford
characters.description: Izzy Langford runs New York's most prestigious debutante ball with an iron fist and an obsessive eye for perfection. Every detail must be flawless, and every young woman must be immaculate. And Izzy knows firsthand what can happen when things go wrong. Decades ago, during her own debut, wealthy and spoiled Sterling Barlowe publicly humiliated her in a scandal that left her reputation in tatters and her family disgraced. Now, Sterling has returned, buying his daughter Plum's entry into the very ball Izzy has spent years perfecting. For Izzy, this isn’t just another debutante season; it’s the opportunity she has waited a lifetime for. Plum will have her perfect debut, but Sterling himself? He will be making his final bow. Izzy is the antagonist of "Deadutante". Best Served Cold: After Sterling forces Plum into the following year's ball, Izzy takes the year to plot her revenge, setting up events so that she could murder Sterling and pin it on someone else. Control Freak:Verymeticulous about the debutante ball she directs. Fake Alibi: Has her assistant Jules see her looking for replacement gloves in the office so she'll think she was there when Sterling was murdered. It fails because Izzy wasn't there when Jules left a note about changing a guest's title, causing a stir when she addresses him wrong.

characters.name: Rachel Withers
characters.description: "Always the bridesmaid, never the bride" is an expression Rachel Withers would understand better than most women. She is the friend who always shows up for baby showers, bridal parties, and milestone birthdays. You name it; she's planned, organized, and celebrated it. When Rachel finally has something worth celebrating—an inheritance of a villa from a late relative—she throws herself a party, expecting her friends to return the favor just once. No one comes.
