Devastated, Rachel confronts her best friend, Kimberly, the woman she's stood beside through three marriages and countless life events. That's when she learns that Kimberly not only skipped the party but also told their entire social circle to blow it off. The confession inspires Rachel to plan another big event: Kimberly's funeral. Rachel is the antagonist of "Otherwise Enraged". A Birthday, Not a Break: Kimberly's (third) marriage was on Rachel's 30th birthday, which Rachel holds against her. Control Freak: The reason she plans so many parties for people isn't so much out of kindness but because she wants to manage everything. Drowning My Sorrows: Having no one come to her party prompts her to drink more and more. By the end she's drinking champagne straight from the bottle.

characters.name: Elliott Pope
characters.description: Elliot Pope is a literary institution, with sixteen bestsellers and a mountain of accolades. Yet his lifelong friend, Barney Corman—a bookstore owner and critic from their hometown of Massapequa—has always recused himself from reviewing Elliot's work to preserve his objectivity. That boundary collapses one night when Barney offers to critique an unpublished manuscript. After months of agonizing silence, Barney finally delivers his verdict, and it is brutal. So brutal that Elliot decides to bury the critique alongside the critic. Elliott is the antagonist of "Murder, He Wrote." Can't Take Criticism: It's safe to say Elliott is pathologically unable to handle criticism of his work. He murders Barney after Barney tells him his honest opinion of the draft form of the book he's working on, despite that Elliott himself insisted on hearing it after Barney initially didn't want to tell him. Also at his first reading Elsbeth attends as well, he's very sensitive about the questions she asks. Creative Sterility: His work isclearly based on his own life, and he is not good at making things up. Creature of Habit: His habit of licking his thumb before turning a page is what ultimately busts him, as the DNA from his saliva is found on Barney's rare copy ofHowards End.

characters.name: Dr. Mallory Haynes
characters.description: Dr. Mallory Haynes makes a point of being there for Manhattan's elite. As a wealth therapist, she is paid handsomely to soothe anxieties, explore feelings, and listen to a wide range of problems. What Mallory's clients don't know is that while they're pouring out their privileged hearts, she's mining their confessions for valuable financial data. No one is the wiser until Jason Rathbone, an aviation heir under SEC scrutiny, connects the dots. Faced with professional ruin and a prison sentence if Jason carries out his threat to expose her, the none-too-good doctor decides it's time to end the therapist-patient relationship. Mallory is the antagonist of "High Class Problems." Awesome by Analysis: She is a deeply perceptive woman, to the extent that she can trade on the stock market without her patients even mentioning their business directly. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Mallory is using her patients as a means of illegally lining her pockets and using her stockbroker boyfriend's accounts to do so, not to mention being perfectly willing to frame him for the trading when it gets exposed and then dump him. Driven by Envy: Being surrounded byfar wealthier peopledrove her to insider trading to get ahead. When Jason tells her she'll never be one of them, it strikes a nerve.

characters.name: Juliet Woodbent
characters.description: Tradwife influencer Juliet Woodbent prides herself on doing it all. She's built a reputation around her picture-perfect life with her husband, Grant, and their six children, a life that conveniently omits the million-dollar startup she sacrificed for domestic bliss. A life that she's gone to great lengths to protect. When up-and-coming filmmaker Audra Miller, who's been documenting the Woodbent family, catches Juliet feeding lard to Grant's vegan boss and later venting her rage and announces plans to release the footage, Juliet realizes there's only one recipe left in her arsenal. Juliet is the antagonist of the episode "Murder From Scratch". Awful Wedded Life: She tries to hide it, but her marriage isn't a good one. Not only is she totally stressed out by being a tradwife, but her husband, Grant, is a misogynistic prick who thinks that all women were born to serve men. Female Misogynist: As part of being a tradwife, she looks down on more independent women. Feminine Women Can Cook: She purposely invokes this trope and tries to make other women like Audra and Elsbeth feel bad for not living up to that ideal. That said, she is a genuinely good cook.

characters.name: Betty Heymouth
characters.description: Betty Heymouth is a long-running gossip columnist atNew York Viewwith a long career. While she comes across as old school, she has a secret which is worth killing for. Something which talk show host Otis Langley finds out the hard way when he threatens to reveal it unless she prints what he wants. In her own words,"Nobody tells Betty Heymouth what to print." Betty is the antagonist of the episode "Catch and Kill". Audience Shift: Defied. She tried to appeal to a younger audience with her column by covering more recent celebrities, but backlash from her established fanbase caused theNew York Viewto reel that back. So Betty had to find another outlet. …But He Sounds Handsome: Inverted. Betty insults Pop Lunatic in her column as modern drivel while secretly being the owner of the account. Did You Just Romance Cthulhu?: She apparently had a fling withAugusto Pinochet(realnice guy,by the way), which is where she got the Soviet pistol to shoot Otis and frame Lorena with. She also apparently had some kind of relationship withPanama dictator Manuel Noriega.

characters.name: Ruby Lane
characters.description: Cabaret legend Ruby Lane is proud to call the Hotel Reilly, one of Manhattan's best hotels, home. She doesn't just do two shows a night at the Reilly; she lives there. Of course, she's not as wealthy as she used to be, but that's not a problem. Until fellow resident Duke Sebastian Mason flies in from England to cast the deciding vote on whether to sell the building. Afraid that her mounting debts will be exposed and that she'll be thrown out if the Duke votes yes, Ruby decides to have him check out early, by using her trophy for more than showing off. Ruby is the antagonist of "That's All''. Fake Alibi: Claimed to have been watching an episode ofFather Crimewhere she appeared, but she didn't know her big scene got cut. Lady Drunk: Subverted. Ruby appears to have a drinking problem that causes her to forget her lines while she sings, but that's only an act to make herself more memorable to her audiences. Mock Millionaire: The reason behind her having killed Sebastian. The sale of the building and the subsequent auditing for its long-standing residents would have revealed how deep in the red she really was and thus given her the boot.

characters.name: Olivia Cherry
characters.description: Olivia is the victim of "Pilot". Make It Look Like A Suicide: Prof. Modarian stages her death this way, but Elsbeth isn't fooled because she had just used teeth whitener and had in her diaphragm. Slain in Their Sleep: Drugged with sleeping pills before being suffocated. Teacher/Student Romance: Had one with Prof. Modarian before he moved on to another student.

characters.name: Gloria Blecher
characters.description: Gloria is the victim of "A Classic New York Character". Asshole Victim: Gloria Blecher is the co-op board president of an apartment building who drives everyone crazy with her interference, from trying to set up someone with her son to interrupting a kid's birthday party over the noise to refusing to sell or renovate to openly threaten them with blackmail to ensure she stays in control—and potentially poisoned the dog that one previously owned too. It's no wonder that pretty much everyone on the building board aided Joann Lenox in setting up her murder. Also, when tearing up Gloria's apartment, they find the remains of her husband who "ran off" 30 years earlier—so on top of everything else, she was a killer herself. Bad People Abuse Animals: When she and the others get busted in the end, Joann says to Dorothy that she knows in her heart of hearts that Gloria poisoned her first dog Bubbles. Considering how awful a person Gloria was, it doesn't sound implausible. Ceiling Banger: Gloria does this to Daniel when his daughter's friends are singing "Happy Birthday" to her, one of the many things that establishes Gloria as an utter bitch. Constructive Body Disposal: As Gloria's apartment is being renovated, breaking the wall reveals the corpse of her supposedly disappeared husband.

characters.name: The Second "A Classic New York Character" Victim
characters.description: Lewis is the secondary victim of "A Classic New York Character". Constructive Body Disposal: As Gloria's apartment is being renovated, breaking the wall reveals the corpse of her supposedly disappeared husband, Lewis. Death by Woman Scorned: It's revealed that Gloria killed him after discovering his affair with Sadie. Hanky-Panky with the Help: Lewis was sleeping with Sadie Grozeki, Joann's mother, who was also working as their maid. Posthumous Character: He's been dead for over 30 years by the time his corpse is discovered.

characters.name: Wendy Wexler
characters.description: Wendy is the victim of "Reality Shock". Alliterative Name:WendyWexler, who, for bonus points, stars on a show calledLavishLadies. Bad Influencer: Wendy is aThe Real Housewives-type star that does Cameos and indulges inProduct Placementwhile also being a drug dealer with a particular line inMother's Little Helpers. She used those to ruin Katricia's life at Skip's request, causing her to lose custody of her kids. She alsopromised to give Katricia something to make it up to her...a discount coupon for one of her blenders. Bathing Beauty: Her last Cameo, at the end of her life, has her in a bubble bath. Blackmail Backfire: Threatens Skip that she'll inform the police about him having drugged Katricia unless he gives her more creative control. Instead, he silences her permanently.

characters.name: "Gabriel"
characters.description: Gabriel is the victim of "Love Knocked Off". Burial at Sea: Margo drops Dennis/Gabriel's body in the water at the Hamptons. Con Artist: Dennis is a petty crook who was picked out by Margo to pretend to be a multi-millionaire to seduce Lainey. Death by Irony: Dennis/Gabriel, aCon Artist, is killed by beingBludgeoned to Deathwith an imitation Cupid statue by matchmaker Margo. Fake Australian: In-universe. Dennis is a New Jerseyan who pretends to be Australian Gabriel Erwood.

characters.name: "Yo-Yo" Arnaldo
characters.description: Yo-Yo is the victim of "Ball Girl". In-Universe Nickname: Johann's is "Yo-Yo". Latin Lover: Yo-Yo is a Spanish player with a thick accent who is shown all over his girlfriend in his first scene.

characters.name: Dr. Olsen
characters.description: Dr. Astrid is the victim of "An Ear for an Ear". Bad Influencer: She is a plastic surgeon but with a heavy social media presence, whocriticizes her co-workers onlineand appeals to fellow influencers. Cruel and Unusual Death: That final injection to the spleen came after being injected 22 other timesin the face. Ouch, to put it mildly. Plastic Bitch: Dr Olsen is a plastic surgeon who is openly rude and disparaging to her co-workers.

characters.name: Derek Davis
characters.description: Derek is the victim of "Something Blue". Alliterative Name:DerekDavis. Bound and Gagged: Ashton taped Derek to the steering wheel and gagged him with dissoluble tape. The gagging backfires on him, when Derek suffocates before he can drown, which tips off the police that Derek's death was suspicious. Have You Told Anyone Else?: Hayes clarifies that Derek hasn't told anyone about his discovery of the company's criminal ways. Derek foolishly confirms he hasn't. Loose Lips: Derek is murdered because he immediately starts telling people about his father-in-law'sWhite-Collar Crime.

characters.name: Josh Johnson
characters.description: Josh is the victim of "Artificial Genius". Alliterative Name:JoshJohnson. Bludgeoned to Death: After she shocks Josh a few times with her cattle prod, Quinn finishes him off by bashing his head with the handled end. Intrepid Reporter: He set out to expose Cerberus as fraudulent, which cost him his life.

characters.name: Gonzo
characters.description: Gonzo was Josh Johnson's dog, a purebred Border Terrier, who was used in Quinn's plot to murder Josh. She planted the ruse of a dognapper in the area who focused on purebreds, and after killing Josh, dognapped Gonzo and abandoned her in a nearby park. Luckily Gonzo was recovered and adopted by Elsbeth. Gonzo is a minor victim of "Artificial Genius". The Dog Bites Back: After being dognapped by Quinn, Gonzo found the incriminating headband that landed Quinn in jail. Meaningful Name: Gonzo's prior owner was a journalist, and "gonzo journalism" refers to a highly subjective journalism style.

characters.name: Gemma Nelson
characters.description: When Joe Dillon learned from his regular/crush Ivy Benson about being triggered by the knowledge that Gemma Nelson, who bullied her in college so much that Ivy had to drop out, had become a successful entrepreneur, Joe sought to avenge Ivy by tracking Gemma home and strangling her in her sleep. Except it was Jane Dunhill, the woman who was staying in Gemma's apartment on a trip to New York, which was unlucky for Jane...and for those around Gemma. Gemma was the target of "Sweet Justice", but Jane Dunhill was killed in her place. Alpha Bitch: Was this to Ivy in college, and completely selfish and entitled to this day. Asshole Victim: Would be if she had been the one killed. Hate Sink: Even Elsbeth has nothing nice to say about her.

characters.name: Jane Dunhill
characters.description: Jane was a beloved teacher and hospital volunteer from a small Indiana town who decided to make a solo trip to New York. Jane's friend Brad agreed to do a house swap, to which Brad's girlfriend Gemma Nelson reluctantly agreed. Sadly, the night Jane was in town happened to be the night Joe Dillon showed up to wreak revenge on Gemma for how she treated Ivy Benson. Jane is the victim of "Sweet Justice". Innocent Bystander: The first victim on the show who had no previous history with their killer. Murder by Mistake: She died because Joe found her sleeping in Gemma's apartment and figured she was Gemma. Slain in Their Sleep: Was strangled while asleep.

characters.name: Ezra Tate
characters.description: Ezra Tate is the primary victim of "A Fitting Finale". Blackmail Backfire: Ezra planned to blackmail Nadine with the pictures of the Pangaea Project. The attempt got him killed by Matteo. The Gambling Addict: Ezra had debts from gambling, which prompted him to blackmail Matteo. In the Back: How Ezra was killed by Matteo. Leeroy Jenkins: Ezra was apparently always very impulsive, and didn't evenKnow When to Fold 'Em. The latter got him killed.

characters.name: Bobby Domingo
characters.description: Bobby Domingo is the secondary victim of "A Fitting Finale". Bludgeoned to Death: Bobby was bludgeoned by Matteo with a fire poker.

characters.name: Eddie Reese
characters.description: A Wall Street type who recently inherited his grandmother's subscription to the opera, Eddie Reese saw it as one thing: a good way to get women in bed. Show after show, he quickly drew the ire of patron Phillip Cross, and met his end after one crude disruptive act too many. Eddie is the victim of the episode "Subscription to Murder". Asshole Victim: Eddie was an insufferable douche who took multiple women to bed from his opera seats. Disproportionate Retribution: As much of a boorish and disruptive ass as he was, getting stabbed more than 10 times, or of course,anytimes, is pretty harsh. Disrupting the Theater: He and his companions broke pretty much every theater taboo one could think of, including taking a call during the show, which turned out to be Phillip's last straw.

characters.name: Gavin Morrissey
characters.description: One of a team of billionaires set to go into space following training, green energy titan Gavin Morrissey felt on top of the world. Unable to resist a few digs in at his buddy Neal Dorsey, those taunts led him to his doom when he stepped into the centrifuge, unaware he would die a fiery death in it. Gavin is the victim of the episode "The Wrong Stuff." Asshole Victim: Not only did he pick on others at training, he also profited off not-so-green ventures. Broken Pedestal: Randy is devastated to learn that Gavin made money off of anti-environmental businesses. Cruel and Unusual Death: One has to hope that explosion took him out quickly...

characters.name: Sonny Miller
characters.description: Sonny is the victim of the episode "Devil's Night". Blackmail Backfire: He tried to muscle his way in on Danny stealing Mac's money, and only got a bullet as his prize.

characters.name: Claude Tobia
characters.description: The rare gem expert of Vivienne's Jewelry, Claude seemed to be an ideal candidate for customer Roselyn Bridwell's plan to rob the joint. One of his coworkers (and Roselyn's inside woman) cited recent money troubles and leaving a meeting with the new head Valentina as a reason he'd be onboard with "verifying" Roselyn's borrowed necklace as the real deal while the jewels were swapped out with fakes. Unfortunately, Claude had actually been crying in happiness of Valentina promoting him, and thus he happily told Roselyn to her face he'd rat her out, forcing her to permanently shut him up. Claude is the victim of the episode "Diamonds Are for Elsbeth". He Knows Too Much: Roselyn goes to Claude looking to bring him in on the caper, but when he gleefully reveals to her that he actually likes Valentina and plans to turn her in, she thinks fast and poisons him. Tampering with Food and Drink: He dies when Roselyn puts a spoonful of his cyanide containing silver polish into his tea. Tears of Joy: While Judith reports to Roselyn that Claude was crying after a meeting with Valentina, making it seem like he'd be a viable addition to the gang, he clarifies that he was experiencing these, in response to being promoted. Oops.

characters.name: Jordan Humphries
characters.description: For two years, prep cook Jordan had been waiting to advance from his downstairs position, growing increasingly restive and openly defiant of his boss, Genevieve "Veev" Hale. With this resentment in mind, he worked out an extra source of income by selling seats at the restaurant online. When he intentionally double-books the restaurant on a night when an important guest is planning to eat there, Veev severely beats him. He announces that he intends to release the cell footage of the beating online, ruining her reputation. This proved to be his greatest mistake, as it lead to his own demise. Jordan is the victim of "Elsbeth Flips the Bird". Asshole Victim: After a certain point he's just trying to destroy Chef Veev for the sake of it. Veev kills Jordan after he illicitly sells reservations, actively tries to sabotage her business and the opportunity to make a franchise deal with a hotel chain, and is generally unpleasant. Batman Gambit: He deliberately riles Veev up to get him to attack her, which he records on his phone so he can upload it and tank her reputation. Unfortunately, he makes the very unwise move of telling her this instead of just leaving, ending up strangled for the efforts. Bullying a Dragon: By the time he's threatening to release footage of Veev beating him up, he already knows she's stronger than she looks, and it's always been obvious she has a temper.

characters.name: Dirk Dashers
characters.description: Dirk is the victim of "Gold, Frankincense, and Murder" Actor Allusion: This is not Christopher Fitzgerald's first foray into a villainous role insomething set around Christmastime.*Just one without as muchhuman trafficking, inciting terrorism, and working with the servants of a demon. Alliterative Name: He even lampshades this, calling his andDeeDee'snames "Alliteration heaven". Asshole Victim: Dirk Dashers was willing to murder his wife so as to not only save his business from the bad image of a divorce, but grow it from the sympathy he'd get for being a Christmas "widower".DeeDeemerely turned his plan against him. Bad Influencer: When Christmas-themed influencer Dirk found out his wifeDeeDeewas leaving him (when he was already cheating on her), he concocted a plan to murder her andMake It Look Like an Accidentin an effort to keep his brand going with a "sympathy bump."

characters.name: Andy Mertens
characters.description: Andy is the victim of the episode "One Angry Woman". His past and death end up being relevant to the Judge Crawford arc in Season 2. Batter Up!: He gets his head knocked in with a baseball bat. That actually ends up throwing a wrench into Crawford's plan, as the bat is signed by a New York player, making it something neither he nor Delia would ever even look at asdie hard Red Sox fans. Dark and Troubled Past: He was blackmailed by Crawford into staying silent on Sherry's death. He Knows Too Much: Andy has apparently been keeping quiet about something Milton was involved with for some time, but for reasons the episode leaves unknown (later revealed to be the murder of Sherry Mitchell), Milton can no longer trust Andy to keep quiet and resolves to make sure hecan'ttell anyone. Oblivious to Love: Teen Andy didn't realize that Sherry was really into him, though he liked her well enough.

characters.name: Cal Reed
characters.description: Cal is the victim of "Toil and Trouble". 0% Approval Rating: When asked if anyone on the crew would want Cal dead, his assistant just pulls out theentirecrew list. Asshole Victim: If his callousness toward Regina wasn't enough, no one else liked working with him. Bad Boss: Throughout Elsbeth and Kaya's interviews of the cast and crew, they find that most everyone thought Cal was a massive dickhead.Pete:Cal was a relic from a bygone era, when people like him could get away with treating others like dirt. Dirty Old Man: The fact that he wasn't worried about his masseuse putting handcuffs on him indicates the massage in question was going to be of thehappy endingvariety.

characters.name: Cole Campbell
characters.description: Cole is the victim of "Unalive and Well." Abusive Parents: He and June are implied to have had them, since they agreed to be paid off about June's death by Tom Murphy. Alcohol-Induced Stupidity: Under the influence of Tom's drugs, Cole tells him that his real name isn't Billy, that he hates Tom, and that his little sister was June, who died on one of Tom's retreats. Alliterative Name: His real name turns out to beColeCampbell. Dead Man Honking: Cole leaves the retreat and drives away. In the next scene, he starts driving erratically, and then his horn is heard blaring, signalling his death.

characters.name: Bill Hepson
characters.description: Bill is the identical twin of Peter Hepson and co-founder of Hepson Capital. He is the victim of "Finance Bros." Cain and Abel: Peter has always been resentful of their mother's favoritism to Bill. This becomes worse when Bill gains a generous reputation and threatens Peter's reputation as well as Hepson Capital's, prompting Peter to kill him. Defector from Decadence: After a near-death experience, Bill has an existential crisis and decides to live humbly, going to extremes to give away his former wealth. Destination Defenestration: How Bill meets his end, he's thrown out of the window.

characters.name: Hayley Ritter
characters.description: Hayley is the first victim of "Tiny Town." Master of the Mixed Message: Hayley refused to do couples' counseling with her boyfriend but still went to haveIVF. It's possible that it was to get some results out that weren't linked to the lab, but that is never said. Mistaken for Romance: Everyone who saw them describes the two as if they were dating. However, both of them had boyfriends, with George's in particular confirming he had no attraction to women. Considering Hayley's method of choice for concealing the flash drive was a box of chocolates, it can be assumed that they intentionallyExploitedthe trope to avoid unwanted attention. Recovered Addict: Hayley had drug problems in the past but had gotten clean. Thorwald claims that she failed a drug test at work, but this is given the lie by the results of an IVF screening from the day after that test. The Stool Pigeon: Hayley was a whistleblower attempting to expose how Elle-Même's concealer was dangerous.

characters.name: George Singh
characters.description: George is the second victim of "Tiny Town." Bury Your Gays: George is a gay man who was murdered, although not for his sexuality but for his job as anIntrepid Reporter. Celebrity Crush: He is suggested to have a crush onNicole Kidman. Fake Mixed Race: Singh is most commonly an Indian name, but George is a white man. He Knows Too Much: Hayley was murdered to keep her from revealing some sort of carcinogen in the company's concealer, with George following suit since he was the reporter she turned to in order to get the truth out.

characters.name: Ethan Brooks
characters.description: Ethan Brooks was director of admissions and the fencing coach at New York's elite Baden University, but he wasn't happy with how his life turned out, and blamed Lawrence Grey, head of Outmatch Educational Consulting, of which his parents were clients. Lawrence decided to settle it with a fencing match. Despite Ethan's swordsmanship Lawrence was easily able to exploit Ethan's foible — his asthma. Ethan is the victim of "Foiled Again". Asthma Peril: Invoked. Ethan has severe asthma, and Lawrence hides his inhaler, lines his fencing mask with cat hair, and convinces him to fence with him. This kills him. Cruel and Unusual Death: His death is a bit more drawn out than most victims on Elsbeth. He dies from his asthma leaving him unable to breathe, with Lawrence even stepping on his chest to help him along. Dies Wide Open: His eyes are open in shock when his body is being zipped up.

characters.name: The Would-Be Second "Foiled Again" Victim
characters.description: Lawrence Grey's cat, from which he got the dander used to kill Ethan Brooks. Lawrence claimed Veritas was already dead to avoid suspicion, and even showed his daughter Mandy Veritas' urn. But Elsbeth realized Lawrence loved his cat too much to kill him, and Mandy found him at a shelter, which provided the evidence needed for Elsbeth to win her game of cat and mouse against Lawrence. Though it initially appears that Veritas is the second victim of "Foiled Again", luckily he is not killed. Faking the Dead: Lawrence pretends Veritas is dead to cover his tracks. Meaningful Name: Named for the motto for Harvard University, the Latin word for "truth," and is key to unravelling Lawrence's lies. Right-Hand Cat: To Lawrence.

characters.name: Nathan Jordan
characters.description: Nathan is the victim of "Tearjerker". The Bad Guy Wins: While he doesn't actually succeed at framing his estranged wife and her lover, they do end up in debt from the lawsuits against him and his "consultant" who served as his accomplice is confident she will get by with it. Didn't Think This Through: A number of elements of his building are dysfunctional, such as the building swaying in the wind or the garbage chute making a lot of noise. Driven to Suicide: He decides to end his life due to suffering from various ailments and to hurt his estranged wife. Spiteful Suicide: His death at Chloe's hands is not murder per se, but rather a suicide meant to frame his wife and her lover and keep them away from his money.

characters.name: Goldie Moresco
characters.description: Goldie is the primary victim of "Scenes From an Italian Restaurant" Asshole Victim: Goldie Moresco was a mobster who refused to acknowledge Pupetta's child as his and accused her of sleeping around, driving her to murder him on the spot. Improvised Weapon: He was stabbed in the chest with a corkscrew thathappened to be on the bar. Only Known by Their Nickname: Goldie's nickname came from his blond hair and mustache, but the characters never refer to him by his birth name. Porn Stache: Buzz Fleming describes his moustache as a "pornstache" that was apparently very popular with the ladies.

characters.name: Eddie Nova
characters.description: Deceased Fall-Guy Gambit: Pupetta repeatedly describes Eddie as Goldie's murderer, as he had been dead for decades. Pupetta is Goldie's actual killer. Fall Guy: Pupetta used his signature double tap to the chest to pin the murder on him. Frame-Up: He was made the scapegoat for Goldie's murder. Posthumous Character: Like Goldie, he's been dead for over 25 years now. The Scapegoat: Pupetta pinned her murder of Goldie on Eddie Nova, triggering a war between the Nova and Del-Ponte crime families that destroyed the former and almost wiped out the latter as well.

characters.name: Gene Genetti, Sr.
characters.description: Gene would have been a victim of "Scenes From an Italian Restaurant", but luckily he survives the attempt on his life. Alliterative Name:GeneGenetti. Evil Parents Want Good Kids: He wanted Gene Jr. to go straight, but Pupetta didn't, which led to her trying to have Gene Sr. run down by a car. False Confession: Confesses to Goldie's murder so the body can be exhumed and the true killer will be known. Fortunately it works. Happily Adopted: Gene Jr. knows Gene Sr. isn't really his father but accepts him as his dad anyway.

characters.name: Tim Pierson
characters.description: After his production company and marriage failed, Tim Pierson returned home, where the only path for him was to run his late father George's snack-food company, Butterwell Treats. Tim wasn't too pleased that his stepmother, Phyllis, was spending a bundle on seeing psychic Marilyn Gladwell, especially when she convinced Phyllis that George wanted her to sell the business. What Tim didn't predict was how far Marilyn would go to keep a lucrative client. Tim is the victim of "I See... Murder". Attack on the Heart: He bites it courtesy of an arrow to the heart. Jerkass: The way he effectively orders his stepmother into not selling the company, as well as the fact he never really cared for it until his film career skidded out, his "recently passed aunt" pickup lines and using his stepmother's chauffeur for his dates without her permission suggest he is not a particularly nice person to be around. Jerkass Has a Point:... not that the above makes him wrong about the fact that Marilyn is ripping Phyllis off in any way.

characters.name: Axel Frostad
characters.description: Axel is the victim of "Hot Tub Crime Machine". Cheated Death, Died Anyway: It turns out Freya has been trying to knock off Axel for months in a variety of "accidents" that he managed to survive. Cruel and Unusual Death: He drowned after Freya clogged the drain with his hair, hislong hairgot stuck in it, and he slowly drowned.

characters.name: Russell Greene
characters.description: Russell is the victim of "Four Body Problem". Conspiracy Theorist: Russell runs a conspiracy theory social media channel and believes in things like wrapping your phone in tinfoil to keep it from being tapped, harassing his own family to get confirmation that his theory that Longacre's funeral was a cover up. The Cuckoolander Was Right: While a lot of his conspiracy theories are outlandish, he was right that something was covered up at N.D. Longacre's funeral. He just wasn't right aboutwhatwas covered up, believing she was still alive. Dead Man Writing: He made a video claiming he'd be killed for hisconspiracy theoriesthat uploaded automatically after he disappeared due to Arthur's murder. Shovel Strike: Arthur knocks him out cold with a shovel to load him into the coffin.

characters.name: Sherry Mitchell
characters.description: In the year 1992, Sherry Mitchell was a young woman born and raised in Stockport, Massachusetts. One summer, she gained a major crush on an employee of the town's yacht club, Andy Mertens. Close to the end of that summer, she entered the yacht club after hours thanks to Andy's keys. Unfortunately for her, a local young rich man known as Milton Crawford with eyes for her tagged along, and when he made a move, she shut him right down. This proved to be her last act, as Milton drowned her in the pool. This lead to a string of events that caused Milton to kill once more... Sherry is the victim of "I Know What You Did Thirty-Three Summers Ago". Blood Is Squickier In Water: Her blood is shown drifting to the top after her murder at Crawford's hands. Fan Disservice: Was murdered and left floating face down in a pool (with her blood at the surface to boot) while wearing a bikini. Plot-Triggering Death: Her murder at Crawford's hands kickstarts his story arc, and lead to the deaths of Andy and Crawford himself years later.

characters.name: Prince Wilhelm
characters.description: Prince Von Hofer is the victim of "I've Got a Little List". Affluent Ascetic:Subverted. Though he may have looked like your average New Yorker, the prince's "poor core" shoes cost $1800 and he lived in a very luxurious van while staying in New York. Innocent Bystander: He just happened to cross Rod's path when he was looking for someone to kill that he deemed expendable. Modest Royalty: Von Hofer wanted to be among the common people instead of staying in fancy hotels, which is unfortunately what got him killed. King Incognito: Von Hofer was the prince of Lichtenburg, but because he was slumming it with the poor while in New York, he dressed in simple clothes and high tops (albeit high tops that cost more than some apartments). Rod killed him based on his looking grungy, not thinking he could be important, which Kaya uses this against Rod in her"Reason You Suck" Speech.

characters.name: The Prison Victim
characters.description: Prof. Modarian is the victim of "Ramen Holiday". For entries related to his first appearance, see his folder under Culprits, above. Asshole Victim: Aside from being a murderer, Alex was hated by the other inmates for his arrogance and lechery. The "Suspect Tango" song even lampshades it: "He had it coming!" Back for the Dead: Alex Modarian, the murderer of the pilot episode, is now himself the murder victim. Blackmail Backfire: In “Ramen Holiday,” he threatens to rat out Mama Martin's smuggling racket and thinks that being in a highly controlled and monitored prison will protect him, even from the warden. He is fatally mistaken. He Knows Too Much: Warden Martin killed Alex because he was about to inform the district attorney about her smuggling operation at the prison.

characters.name: Scotty Bristol
characters.description: Scotty is the victim of "Yes, and...?". Asshole Victim: Scotty was a disrespectful host, a mean boss, a plagiarist, an attempted adulterer, and a bad friend, but still, getting strangled with your own tie bysomeone you thought you could trustis rough. Mean Boss: Bristol likes to shred his writing staff's work in front of them just to make them feel bad, then steal jokes from amateur comedians without giving them credit. Signing-Off Catchphrase: Discussed and played straight. Scotty ends each show by loosening his tie and saying, "It is way late. Go to sleep, everybody. Bye-bye." The fact that his tie was tightened when he got strangled by the shredder clues Elsbeth in that he wasn't alone. Took a Level in Jerkass: He was close friends with Laurel and Mickey back in their college days, but all the fame brought out a meaner and uglier side to him.

characters.name: The Second "Yes, and...?" Victim
characters.description: Mickey is the secondary victim of ''Yes, and...?" Boss's Unfavorite Employee: Mickey gets the brunt of the mockery both from Scotty and the other writers, which Laurel hates. The shredder is even named after him because "it takes the same amount of crap from Scotty". Henpecked Husband: Downplayed. Between and his wife, his wife seems to be the more forceful of the two. While she is protective and cares deeply for him, she's also not unwilling to throw him under the bus to save herself. Hollywood Heart Attack: While his heart issues were foreshadowed, Mickey is talking to Laurel one minute and collapsing from a heart attack the next, with aSmash Cutto him getting zipped up in a body bag.

characters.name: Patrick Palmer
characters.description: Parker Palmer worked at Barker's Toys. Parker is the victim of "Doll Day Afternoon". Alliterative Name:PatrickPalmer. Asshole Victim: Charged 15 times the market price for a Spirited Girl Doll on the black market, then switched specific dolls on the buyer, Nolan, at the last minute. This started a fight that got him killed by accident. Death by Falling Over: He snuffs it when Nolan grabs at him to get his money back, and in the process, sends him crashing onto a cement barrier.

characters.name: The Second "Doll Day Afternoon" Victim
characters.description: Chrissie is the secondary victim in "Doll Day Afternoon". Flat Character: As expected, being an inanimate doll. Mourning an Object: The episode ends on a shot of the doll doctor sadly covering her body with a cloth. Shoot the Hostage: Parodied. Nolan used all of the remaining hostages as a human shield, knowing the police wanted him dead. The group deliberately put Chrissie, with a hat on her head, up higher so she would be most likely to take the sniper's bullet.

characters.name: Johnny Drabowski
characters.description: Johnny is the victim of "Good Grief". Cement Shoes: Well, sandbags in a travel bag that gets clipped to his belt loop in this particular case, but they both get about the same results. Cheated Death, Died Anyway: Survived his helicopter crash (actually never got on it and let everyone think he was dead to get away from Raquel), only to be actually killed by her. Faking Amnesia: He tells Raquel he lost his memory to explain why he didn't come home sooner, but in truth, he had decided to live his life free from her until seeing Raquel's grief (and profit from said grief) on television. Gold Digger: Seeing as Johnny spent his time in Puerto Rico sleeping with other women and complaining about Raquel, it's heavily implied Johnny came back to her thanks to the money she had racked up from her influencing andBlack Veil.

characters.name: Beryl Nix
characters.description: Beryl was an artsy free spirit who was welcome by all in her small Sleepy Hollow neighboorhood, except for her next door neighbor Sharon. When Sharon's beloved towering maple, of which Beryl disapproved, suddenly died, Beryl was suspected. Shortly afterward, for Halloween, Beryl was in charge of the neighborhood's haunted maze, which included her dressed as Ichabod Crane. Beryl did not know she would meet the same fate. She is the victim of "Ick, A Bod". Blithe Spirit: Beryl's free-spiritedness brightens the lives of everyone around her, except for her controlling neighbor Sharon. Bourgeois Bohemian: She's well-off enough to move to a nice house in Sleepy Hollow on her own salary, but is also the type to paint in her house while naked and throw crazy parties. Sharon describes her as "not even a real artist. She's just rich and bored." Cruel and Unusual Death: Having your head cut off is one thing, having it cut off with a chainsaw is probably so much worse.

characters.name: The Towering Maple
characters.description: The Towering Maple is the secondary victim of "Ick, A Bod". Flat Character: Given that it's an inanimate tree, this is a given. Mourning an Object: Sharon had so many memories attached to the tree that she was devastated to see it die. Beryl offered her condolences but Sharon thought she was being insincere. Red Herring: Sharon assumed Beryl, who had toxic chemicals among her art supplies, poisoned the tree. It was actually Sharon's husband, in a misguided attempt to end the feud between them.

characters.name: Delores Feinn
characters.description: Delores was a patron of the Pigeon Press who, in exchange for her support, demanded to be published. She is the victim of "Poetic Justice". Asshole Victim: Given that she freely and willfully deceived people, whether it was pretending to need an oxygen tank so others would give up their seats, or pretending to be extremely wealthy to get journalists to suck up to her by paying for her expensive meals, and publish her horrid writing, Delores wasn't the tiniest bit sympathetic. "Friends" Rent Control: She lived in a spacious, rent-controlled apartment she had been in for decades and for which she only paid two-hundred and fifty dollars a month for, allowing herself to seem much wealthier than she was. Giftedly Bad: It physically pains Gary to have to accept or read her poetry, and one reading of it is clear enough why, such as her "Nipples of the Sea":"Thecerulean, azurewavesCrash into the creamysolar plexusof my eyesThat are also ascreaming mirrorshatteredA pussy willow bleedson the moonor is it a wolfBOTH THINGS CAN BE TRUE"

characters.name: Anders Wittman
characters.description: Anders was a crisis management consultant who was starting to grow a conscience after years of covering up the worst deeds of the rich and famous. Anders is the victim of the episode "Bunker Down". Cheated Death, Died Anyway: Escaped Craig's bunker, only to end up hit by a car. Dying Clue: Scratched a message on a banana in Craig's bunker, naming Craig as his killer. Jerkass: Zigzagged. He worked for a crisis management firm that helps horrid people clean up their messes, but he mentioned he was looking to pivot, possibly out of guilt, so he doesn't quite qualify forAsshole Victimstatus.

characters.name: Alaïa Jade
characters.description: Alaïa Jade was a successful, ifcontroversial, pop star who purchased The Convent of Our Lady of Grace and Mercy, figuring the awe-inspiring building would make a perfect recording studio. The Vatican approved her $27 million offer but not Reverend Mother Constance Mary Cabot, who offered Alaïa, who was uncertain about leaving her longtime producer, to find solace the way she found her calling years before—by viewing the sunset from the bell tower. Hopeful, Alaïa accepted her invitation, unaware how close the not-so-good sister was sending her to Heaven. Alaïa is the victim of "And Then There Were Nuns". Bait-and-Switch Character Intro: The episode begins with her playing aNaughty Nunin a racy and sacrilegious music video, causing Mother Constance to deem her a "Jezebel". But when Alaïa is actually in the church, she comes off as sweet and shy, and mostly focused on coming up with lyrics, not like her promiscuous party girl persona, whichforeshadowsthe fact that the stories about her erratic behavior were fabricated by her producer Shane Sills. Child Popstar: Formerly — Alaïa signed with Shane when she was just 14. Cruel and Unusual Death: As she is coming to peace viewing the sunset, the bell ringing at her sends her into a screaming panic and knocks her headfirst to her death.

characters.name: Dave Coppins
characters.description: Dave was the athletic director at St. Ivan's University, who hired his idol, NBA coach Russell Willoughby to coach the basketball team. When the team was on a losing streak he blamed Coach W's young girlfriend Peyton, which proved to be his biggest mistake. Dave is the victim of "Basket Case". Asshole Victim: Unjustly banned Peyton from the premises, calling Coach W a loser in the process, and laughed when the athletes called Peyton a witch. Broken Pedestal: Dave hired Coach W, a legendary pro, to coach at St. Ivan's in what was supposed to be the highlight of his career. Between the relationship with Peyton and showing his age, Dave was disappointed by the results, leading to him making the overheard insult that got him killed. Dirty Coward: Peyton called him one for not directing his criticism of Coach W toward him, though that didn't make a difference with Coach W bugging the place.

characters.name: Madison Fortune
characters.description: A former model who ran the (S)Heroes modeling agency who was known for her rivalry with Tiff Giles. Madison encouraged Tiff to join her at a reunion in New York City, but unfortunately let it slip that she was culpable for the injury that ended Tiff's modeling career, prompting Tiff to accept, and pay her back in full. She is the victim of "Glamazons". Asshole Victim: Aside from her virtue-signaling, she denied for years her role in Tiff's injury. Crippling the Competition: Downplayed. She's the one who pressured her boyfriend TJ into hurting her rival, Tiff, inspired by theTonya Hardingcase. It was never meant to be such a life-ruining injury, but that didn't stop Madison and TJ from hiding it for 20 years.

characters.name: Donovan Chase
characters.description: Donovan was the avant-garde director-choreographer of the smash hit Broadway musicalOrphan Girl!, who succeeds in pitching a dark revisionist take on the classicThe NutcrackercalledDrosselmeyer's Revengefor the Midtown Ballet Company's annual Christmas show. His vision included a child-free cast, which didn't please board member and dance dad Harris Monroe, as well as a dangerous set piece called "The Contraption," a scary-looking nutcracker head that Harris decided to turn into aDonovan-cracker. Donovan is the victim of "A Hard Nut to Crack". Asshole Victim: Aside from being obnoxiously pretentious andunconcerned with the performers' safety("Safety is the enemy of art!"), he'sdisrespectful toward the crew, berating his assistant while she's out and calling the technical director Kevin instead of his name, Keith. Cruel and Unusual Death: As insufferable as he was, being suddenly crushed by The Contraption is still a horrible way to die. No Celebrities Were Harmed: An edgy modern stage director who utilizes cameras and a walk outside the theater in one of his shows is meant to echo Jamie Lloyd, the director of the 2023 West End revival ofSunset Boulevard, which utilized a similar technique.

characters.name: Tyler Hollis
characters.description: Without anyone to really call family, young Tyler Hollis became effectively a drifter. That all changed when he found work with the wealthy Archer Kopunek, a biohacker who valued his good genetics in his quest to live forever. But after a while, Archer's strict routine made Tyler realize that instead of living forever, all he really wanted to do waslive. Alas, his plans to leave Archer made him much more valuable dead than alive. Tyler is the victim of "Ol' Man Liver". Born Winner: Tyler's great physique is a combination of his youth and good genetics, which is why Archer coveted him so much. Heal It with Blood: Downplayed. Tyler's plasma helps Archer bring down his cellular age, but Archer wasn't exactly ill in the first place. I Just Want to Be Normal: After months of living by Archer's strict health routine, Tyler wants to leave and experience normal life, like drinking a beer or being with a girl. This is unfortunately what gets him killed.

characters.name: Domenico Cappelli
characters.description: Domenico was one of the top wigmakers in New York, who has catered to many stars of stage and screen. When he discovered that one of his colleagues, Felix West, had poached one of his clientsandthat he is using stolen hair to make the wig, he attempted to go mafioso on Felix, but the tables were turned on him. Domenico is the victim of "All's Hair" Blackmail Backfire: When he finds out that Felix stole Lina's business away from him and that he cut hair off of a teenager to do it, he tries to get 40% off of every wig Felix makes from now on, or he will reveal the latter fact to the world. He ends up much the same wayPirelli did when he tried to squeeze Sweeney... dead.noteWhile Domenico's death is more of a "constricted throat" than aSlashed Throat, they both get about the same results. Italian-American Caricature: He lives with his mother, who makes Italian food for his clients during wig fittings. When he discovers Felix's betrayal, he threatens him in a way that makes Felix comment on how hard he is leaning into the Italian stereotype. Meaningful Name: "Cappelli" is the Italian word for hair, and Domenico is an Italian-American wigmaker.

characters.name: The Young Blonde Woman in the Park
characters.description: To get the Molten-Gold hair needed for Lina Vyanti's wig, Felix West cuts off a stranger's ponytail. Shortly afterward, Mitch Newell, a wealthy donor to Captain Wagner's foundation, has the police investigate when he suspects his fourteen-year-old daughter Brynlynn, a dressage rider, has been bullied just before a regional competition. It turns out she was the one Felix had given the unkindest haircut of all. Brynlynn is a minor victim of "All's Hair". Bratty Teenage Daughter: A bit snotty and apathetic, though not as elitist as her father, who chides her for associating with girls from public school. Hairstyle Malfunction: Downplayed. She doesn't look bad in her shortened hair, so it isn't obvious right away that she was Felix's victim. Still, her father wanted her to match her horse for the upcoming competition, and even tried to hire Domenico to make a fake ponytail, but he couldn't do it in time. Innocent Bystander: As soon as Felix sees her molten gold hair, he cuts it off without a second thought. Domenico knew what Felix had done, but didn't mention the fact that she was a fourteen-year-old girl. When Elsbeth reveals this at the end, Felix doesn't seem to care.

characters.name: Morris Long
characters.description: For years, Morris Long had been the editor of the Metropolitan Tribune's crossword puzzle. His use of more modern references and even slang did have a tendency to get under solvers' skin, especially during the crossword tournaments, and none more so than Simon Carroll. When the latter learned he had plans to ask out the recently divorced ElaineMcClusk, who Simon had his sights on, things reached so much of a point that Simon took it upon himself to cross him out for good. Morris is the victim of "Murder Six Across". Jive Turkey: Morris, by hiring younger puzzle makers, actually seems to do a good job of incorporating modern slang and pop culture references into his puzzles, much to the chagrin of the top puzzlers who are all over 35. No Celebrities Were Harmed: Patterned after New York Times crossword puzzle editor Will Shortz, who also runs the largest and oldest crossword tournament in the United States, the American Crossword Puzzle Tournament. Screw the Rules, I Make Them!: After Simon accuses Morris of being unethical by asking a competitor out, Morris points out that he is the one who made the rules, so he can justify that asking a competitor out just for dinner is not technically against the rules. But the very fact that Morris made those rules and is only following them to the letter, not the spirit, just highlights Simon's point, even if it is made out of jealousy.

characters.name: Sterling Barlowe
characters.description: Rich, old-moneyed Sterling Barlowe isn't used to not getting his way. So when Izzy Langford consistently denies his daughter Plum the chance to join New York society, he forces her hand with a sizable donation to secure Plum an invite to the debutante ball the following year. What he doesn't realize is that Izzy harbors a grudge from a cruel prank played decades earlier, and signing that check has also signed his death warrant. Sterling is the victim of "Deadutante". Asshole Victim: In his youth, he humiliated a young woman out of classism, and in the present day uses his wealth to force that same woman (whose name he doesn't even remember) to make his daughter part of the ball in spite of the fact that Izzy is the one to make that decision. All in all, he really earned a sword to the heart. But for Me, It Was Tuesday: When he was a teenager, he used a sword to cut Izzy's dress because she was wearing a dress she couldn't afford and was planning to return after the ball. Once Izzy's speech cuts through and he remembers her, he calls her"Half-Off" instead of her actual name and laughs. Again,earnedthat sword. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: In spite of his horrendous behavior and personality, his daughter Plum is disappointed when she doesn't see him in the crowd during the ball, and she and his third wife are genuinely saddened by his death.

characters.name: Kimberly Brooks
characters.description: Three times married, Kimberly has benefitted from her friend and maid-of-honor Rachel's overeager, controlling nature. When Rachel asks for something in return, Kimberly convinces their friend group to ditch Rachel in order to not "indulge her behavior". But hell hath no fury like a bridesmaid scorned. Kimberly is the victim of "Otherwise Enraged". Alpha Bitch: As the queen bee of the friend group, it just takes one word from Kimberly for everyone to withdraw their RSVP to Rachel's party last minute. Asshole Victim: Rachel may be clingy, controlling, and narcissistic, but Kimberly ensuring that Rachel is all alone on her one big night was downright cruel. Bludgeoned to Death: Died this way via averyexpensive pot.

characters.name: Barney Corman
characters.description: Barney Corman was the owner of Barney's Books, as well as a literary critic and the host of the Authors in Conversation seminar series at the Upper East Side Cultural Center. He grew up with Elliott Pope, and made a point of never publishing his reviews of Elliott's books. When he offered to look at Elliot's latest manuscript, he learned the hard way that Elliott does not take criticism well. Barney is the victim of "Murder, He Wrote". Adoring the Pests: Barney had a fondness for the rat who lives in his store room, naming him Templeton after the rat character fromCharlotte's Web. His wife was not thrilled with this, feeling it was just one more thing that made Barney's store room a death trap, but was happy when Elsbeth invited the humane Rodent Death Society pest controllers to take him away instead of killing him, for the late Barney's sake. Caustic Critic: Played with. His reviews of Elliott's books are scathing, but he's just being honest, and he's right about Elliot being a misogynist who lacks imagination. He also kept those reviews from the public out of respect for their childhood growing up together when he was alive, but once Elsbeth discovers them via Elliot's ex-wife, she mentions plans to publish those scathing reviews in order to keep Barney's wife afloat. There's No Place Like Home: One of Barney's points of criticism for Elliott is how much he not-so-covertly slanders the people they grew up with in Massapequa, showing how much fondness he has for his hometown.

characters.name: Jason Rathbone
characters.description: Heir to a major aircraft manufacturing company on the cusp of taking over from his billionaire father, Jason's ascension is interrupted by a probe from the SEC for insider trading. The only person with the knowledge of his personal life to make the trades? His trusted wealth therapist, Dr. Mal. When he confronts her over this and threatens to torpedo her career, however, he does not anticipate her using her personal knowledge of him to silence him... forever... Jason is the victim of "High Class Problems". Jerkass: Jason arranged for his buildings power to leech off the city lines in the event of a blackout just because he needs his precious sauna so badly. Jerkass Has a Point: That said, he's well within his rights to try and expose Mallory for betraying his trust, especially because said betrayal is having him investigated for a crime he wasn't actually committing. Too Dumb to Live: He tells Mallory face-to-face that he plans to expose her insider trading, a crime that will land her in federal prison and ruin her career, rather than just exposing her and leaving her no time to retaliate. For bonus points, he asks her to his home, which she knows quite a bit about, to do so.

characters.name: Audra Miller
characters.description: A documentary filmmaker whose promising early work has not quite panned out yet, she is paid big money to film tradwife Juliet Woodbent. But Audra is skeptical of her subject's lifestyle and looking for a more authentic, human angle on the overly cheerful Juliet. She gets it when she spots that Juliet accidentally used lard in a meal meant for her husband's vegan boss and wife and gets it on camera. Probably wasn't the best idea to tell Juliet all this, however, since the tradwife decides to make a homemade ammonia cleaner which, when combined with bleach, causes Audra's life to cut to black. Audra is the victim of "Murder from Scratch". Accomplice by Inaction: Discussed. Juliet points out that Audra could have warned herbeforethat she had used lard for a vegan couple, instead of informing her after she had already served the meal just to expose Juliet as human and make a good documentary. Deadly Gas: How Audra dies. She is tricked into mixing Juliet's homemade ammonia cleaner tablet with bleach and is then shut in the bathroom to die by the toxic gas that results. Foil: Unlike Juliet, who keeps everything tidy and makes things from scratch, Audra had a messy apartment and went for convenience, buying premixed Arnold Palmers and precut fruit.

characters.name: Otis Langley
characters.description: Otis Langley is the popular host of talk showNew York Confidential. Otis is the victim of "Catch and Kill". Asshole Victim: Wasnice on camera, but tended to berude to staff, waiters, service people, and more. This was an open secret in New York society, but due to Otis having dirt on everyone nobody exposed him until his death. He also had running prank using the face of the reviled Lorena Marchuk to scare guests. Blackmail Backfire: He blackmails Betty, as he has with a lot of other media personalities, to print whatever he wants. But instead of bowing to the blackmail, Betty shoots Otis in the back, which leads tohis bad reputation going public anyway. No Celebrities Were Harmed: Has some passing gender-flipped similarities toEllen DeGeneresas a gay talk show host with a positive public reputation who was later revealed to not be so nice behind the scenes.

characters.name: Duke Sebastian
characters.description: Sebastian Mason, an English Duke, came to his New York pied-à-terre, the Hotel Reilly, to vote on selling the building. There, hotel resident and regular entertainer Ruby Lane tried to convince him to change his vote but he refused, prompting her to resort to a more persuasive measure. Duke Sebastian is the victim of "That's All". Bludgeoned to Death: Ruby does him in withher own award. Make It Look Like an Accident: Ruby attempts to make it look like he slipped in the shower and cracked his head on the tiles. It ends up screwing her over, as she wasn't strong enough (and the room too well-maintained) to break the towel bar to set the scene she wanted, forcing her to use the hotel's shoehorn to pry it off and her trophy to hammer it, getting the shoehorn's monogram all over the base. The fact that he preferred morning baths to nighttime showers doesn't help. OOC Is Serious Business: Was known to bathe every morning, which makes Elsbeth doubt that he would have showered at night.
